meta.archiveNote: UNREACHABLE at runtime, independent of auth/middleware. Next.js App Router treats any path segment starting with an underscore as a private folder (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/colocation#private-folders) and excludes it from route generation entirely. So app/api/_archive/**/route.js files never become live endpoints — a request to /api/_archive/anything 404s before middleware.js or next.config.js are even consulted for that path. Confirmed by reading next.config.js (no rewrites() or redirects() entry references '_archive') and middleware.js in full (zero string matches for '_archive'; its matcher config only lists '/api/:path*' plus specific pages, and none of the demo-mode dispatch tables, PUBLIC_ROUTES, or hosted-public-path checks mention _archive). scripts/lib/route-sql-guard.mjs explicitly skips the '_archive' directory when walking route files, confirming the team already treats it as inert/excluded tooling-side. Net effect: these 48 archived route files are dead code from a routing standpoint — the handlers themselves are syntactically intact and mostly still reference live schema tables (verified goals, milestones, ideas, contacts, interactions, agent_messages, message_threads, shared_docs, context_points, context_entries, calendar_events, snippets, user_observations/preferences/moods/approaches, notification_preferences, workflows, executions, scheduled_jobs, agent_pairings, agent_identities, content, health_snapshots, entities, topics, and feedback all still exist in schema/schema.js), but none of that matters because the folder is never mounted as a route. Un-archiving (renaming _archive -> something routable) would make most of them functional again since they read live tables.

items.purpose: Bulk or single deletion of action records (and their related open_loops/assumptions) by ID(s) or by filter; admin-only, audit-logged.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie; additionally requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin' or 403

inputs.query.action_ids: comma-separated string, optional — bulk delete by exact IDs
inputs.query.before: date string, optional — delete rows with timestamp_start before this (only used if no action_id(s))
inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional filter for bulk-by-filter delete
inputs.query.status: string, optional filter for bulk-by-filter delete

items.errors: 403 non-admin; 400 empty action_ids list or no filter supplied for the generic bulk path
items.gotchas: Generic filter-based delete requires at least one of before/agent_id/status to avoid an accidental full wipe; deletion cascades to open_loops and assumptions rows first, then action_records; every deletion path writes an audit-log entry (action.deleted) via logActivity so the erasure itself is traceable.

items.name: GET /api/actions
items.purpose: Lists governed action records for the org with filtering, paging, and rollup stats; also lazily sweeps expired pending_approval rows to 'expired' before returning results.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role (no admin gate)

inputs.query.swarm_id: string, optional, filter by fan-out session group
inputs.query.status: string, optional; 'pending_approval' triggers the lazy expiry sweep first
inputs.query.days: string/number, optional (1-365), scopes total+stats to a rolling window

items.response: { actions: Row[], total: number, stats: object, lastUpdated: ISO string }
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse on unexpected failure
items.gotchas: When status=pending_approval, expired rows are flipped server-side before the listing query runs and an ACTION_UPDATED bulk event is published if any were swept; this can change which rows are returned vs a naive read.

items.name: POST /api/actions
items.purpose: Creates a new governed action record: validates the payload, resolves agent identity, redacts secrets, checks plan quotas, evaluates the guard/policy engine, and persists the record (or a blocked record if the guard denies it).
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role (no admin gate); agent identity additionally resolved via JWT/signature (resolveAgentIdentity)

inputs.body.agent_id: string, required, max 128 (may be overridden by a verified JWT sub)
inputs.body.action_type: string, required, max 128 (free-form; may be overridden by the guard's evidence-fold)
inputs.body.action_id: string, optional max 128; server generates act_<uuid> if omitted
inputs.body.status: string, optional, one of 'running'|'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'|'pending'|'pending_approval'|'blocked' (defaults to 'running' unless guard requires approval)
inputs.body.risk_score: integer 0-100, optional, client-declared; server takes max(server,client) via guard
inputs.body.timestamp_start: ISO datetime string, optional, defaults to now
inputs.body.cost_estimate: number >=0, optional, clamped to 10000; auto-derived from tokens+model if omitted
inputs.body.idempotency_key: string, optional max 256; replays return the existing row with idempotent_replay:true
inputs.body.guard_decision_id: string, optional, must match /^act_gd_[a-f0-9]{16}$/ and belong to an existing same-org guard decision or 400
inputs.body.harness_session_id / subagent_uuid: string, optional, bounded to <=200 chars else nulled
inputs.body.act: object, optional evidence payload, deep-validated the same way as guard's act field
inputs.body._signature: string, optional RSA signature over the payload (minus _signature) for agent identity verification

items.response: 201 (or 202 if pending_approval): { action, action_id, decision (guard decision object), security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories} }. Idempotent replay: { action, action_id, idempotent_replay: true }.
items.errors: 400 invalid JSON / validation failed / bad guard_decision_id; 402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED (actions or agents); 403 AGENT_NOT_REGISTERED (closed enrollment) or 'Action blocked by policy' (guard block, includes action+decision); 401 SIGNATURE_REQUIRED / INVALI…
items.gotchas: Guard evaluation can rewrite action_type via the evidence fold — the persisted record uses the swapped type. risk_score persisted is the guard's authoritative score (max of server/client), never the raw client value. Side effects fire via after(): meter increments, agent presence heartbeat, background embedding indexing, real-time SSE event, Discord/webhook alerts, digest tick, and a launch-windo…

items.name: GET /api/actions/{actionId}
items.purpose: Fetches a single action with its related open_loops, assumptions, message-summary counts, and linked guard_decision; lazily expires the row if it's an overdue pending_approval.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.response: { action, open_loops: Row[], assumptions: Row[], guard_decision: {...decision, matched_policies, context, evidence} | null }
items.errors: 404 'Action not found'; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: If status is pending_approval and past approval_expires_at, the route flips it to expired in-place (publishing ACTION_UPDATED) before responding — the same lazy-sweep pattern used on the list GET.

items.name: PATCH /api/actions/{actionId}
items.purpose: Updates an action's outcome/progress fields (status, output_summary, tokens, cost, model, etc.); gates 'close' fields against overwriting a terminal state while always allowing token/cost/model updates through.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.body.cost_estimate: number >=0, optional, clamped to 10000; auto-derived from tokens if omitted
inputs.body.model: string, optional max 128; falls back to the row's stored model for cost calc if omitted
inputs.body.close_if_running: boolean, optional — Stop-hook contract; when true, close fields only apply if the row is still status='running'
inputs.body.outcome_metadata.spawned_agent_uuid: string, optional, <=200 chars — persisted into outcome_progress regardless of the close gate

items.response: { action: updated row, security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories}, cost_alert?: {threshold, severity} }
items.errors: 400 invalid/non-object JSON body or validation failed; 404 action not found (no close fields submitted or truly missing); 409 'Action is in a terminal state and cannot be modified' when close fields target an already-terminal row
items.gotchas: At least one recognized outcome field is required by validateActionOutcome or validation fails. Close fields (status/output_summary/timestamp_end) only apply if the row's status is 'running' (or per close_if_running semantics for the Stop hook); non-close fields (tokens/cost/model/side_effects/etc.) always apply even after closure. Also triggers cost-alert evaluation and best-effort learning-epis…

items.name: GET /api/actions/{actionId}/artifacts
items.purpose: Lists artifacts (files/outputs) recorded against a specific action, paged.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.response: { artifacts: shaped artifact rows[], total: number }
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: Does not 404 for an unknown actionId — an action with no artifacts simply returns an empty array with total 0.

items.name: GET /api/actions/{actionId}/graph
items.purpose: Builds a read-only execution graph (nodes + edges) for an action, combining trace data (parent chain, sub-actions, related actions, assumptions, open loops) for the Execution Graph tab on the decision replay page.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.errors: 404 'Action not found'; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: Graph is derived entirely from getActionTraceData (same underlying query set as /trace) — no separate graph storage; edges represent parent-chain, sub-action, related-action, assumption, and open-loop relationships.

items.name: GET /api/actions/{actionId}/messages
items.purpose: Returns agent messages correlated to an action, either explicitly tagged (action_id match) or, as a fallback, matched by agent + time-window overlap; also supports a summary-only mode.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.pathParams.actionId: string, required, must start with 'ar_' or 'act_' or 400
inputs.query.summary: string 'true', optional — returns aggregated stats instead of the full message list

items.response: Summary mode: { total, participants: string[], correlation: 'explicit'|'none', first_message_at, last_message_at }. Normal mode: { messages: Row[] (each tagged with match_type: 'explicit'|'time_window'), correlation: 'explicit'|'time_window'|'none', total }
items.errors: 400 invalid/missing action_id prefix; 500 'Failed to fetch messages'
items.gotchas: Correlation strategy has two tiers — explicit action_id tag wins; only if zero explicit matches does it fall back to a time-window (action.timestamp_start..timestamp_end) join on the same agent_id. No results returns {messages: [], correlation: 'none', total: 0}, not a 404.

items.name: GET /api/actions/{actionId}/outcome
items.purpose: Fetches the terminal outcome fields (status/summary/error/progress/elapsed) for an action from the dedicated outcome columns (distinct from the general action record).
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.response: { action_id, status, outcome_at, summary, error_message, progress, elapsed_ms }
items.errors: 404 'Action not found'; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: elapsed_ms is computed as NOW()-created_at when outcome_at is null (i.e. an in-progress estimate), not just outcome_at-created_at.

items.name: POST /api/actions/{actionId}/outcome
items.purpose: Agent-reported one-shot terminal outcome for an action (completed/partial/failed), with lifecycle gating so blocked/pending/cancelled/failed actions can't have an outcome stamped, and mirrors execution status into an x402 purchase row if one exists.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.body.status: string, required, one of 'completed'|'partial'|'failed' ('lost_confirmation' is reserved for the system sweep and rejected here)
inputs.body.error_message: string, required if status='failed'; truncated to 4000 chars; redacted for secrets
inputs.body.progress: object, required if status='partial'; max 8KB serialized JSON; string values redacted
inputs.body.summary: string, optional; truncated to 4000 chars; redacted for secrets

items.response: { outcome: {action_id, status, outcome_at, summary, error_message, progress, elapsed_ms}, security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories} }
items.errors: 400 invalid status, missing error_message for failed, missing/invalid progress for partial, or progress payload too large; 404 action not found; 409 'Cannot report an outcome for an action in status <status>' (blocked/pending_approval/cancelled/fail…
items.gotchas: One-shot semantics — a second POST for the same action conflicts (409) rather than overwriting. If a matching x402 purchase row exists for this action, its execution_status is synced (completed->succeeded, partial->partial, failed->failed) best-effort (failure to sync is logged, not surfaced to the caller).

items.name: GET /api/actions/{actionId}/trace
items.purpose: Builds a root-cause trace for an action: assumptions, open loops, parent chain, sub-actions, and time/agent-correlated related actions, plus derived root_cause_indicators (invalidated assumptions, open loops, failed parents, related failures).
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.response: { action, trace: { assumptions: {total, validated, invalidated, unvalidated, items}, loops: {total, open, resolved, cancelled, items}, parent_chain, sub_actions, related_actions, root_cause_indicators: [{type, severity, count, detail}] } }
items.errors: 404 'Action not found'; 500 'An error occurred while building the trace'
items.gotchas: related_actions correlation window is agent match OR same non-empty systems_touched, within +/-1 hour of timestamp_start, limited to 20 rows — a heuristic join, not an explicit link.

items.name: GET /api/actions/costs
items.purpose: Returns cost/token aggregation (totals, per-agent breakdown, per-day series, attribution coverage) over a rolling window, excluding x402_purchase actions.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional, scopes all aggregates to one agent

items.response: { total_cost_usd: number, total_tokens_in: number, total_tokens_out: number, period, attribution: {attributed_count, total_count, coverage_pct|null}, by_agent: [{agent_id, cost_usd, action_count, attributed_count, coverage_pct|null}], by_day: [{date, cost_usd, action_count}] }
items.errors: 400 invalid period; 500 on unexpected failure ('Failed to fetch cost data')
items.gotchas: Excludes action_type = 'x402_purchase' rows so spend/purchase actions don't double-count against the governance cost view.

items.name: GET /api/actions/loops
items.purpose: Lists open loops (unresolved follow-ups tied to actions) with filtering, paging, and a status/priority rollup.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.response: { loops: Row[] (each with joined agent_id/agent_name/declared_goal/action_type), total: number, stats: {open_count, resolved_count, critical_open, high_open}, lastUpdated: ISO string }
items.errors: 500 ('An error occurred while fetching open loops', with empty loops/stats)
items.gotchas: Ordered by priority (critical>high>medium>low) then created_at DESC; the count query mirrors the main query's LEFT JOIN to action_records so an agent_id filter (which references the joined table) doesn't break COUNT(*).

items.name: POST /api/actions/loops
items.purpose: Creates an open loop (follow-up item) attached to a parent action; redacts sensitive fields and publishes a real-time LOOP_CREATED event.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.body.action_id: string, required max 128 — parent action must exist in-org or 404
inputs.body.loop_id: string, optional max 128; server generates loop_<uuid> if omitted

items.response: 201: { loop: {...loop row, agent_id, agent_name, declared_goal, action_type from parent action}, loop_id, security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories} }
items.errors: 400 validation failed; 404 'Parent action not found'; 409 duplicate loop_id
items.gotchas: description/owner/resolution are run through redactAny before insert; the response embeds the parent action's agent/goal fields to save the frontend a follow-up fetch.

items.name: GET /api/actions/loops/{loopId}
items.purpose: Fetches a single open loop by loop_id, joined with its parent action's agent/goal/status fields.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role
items.response: { loop: {...row, agent_id, agent_name, declared_goal, action_type, action_status} }
items.errors: 404 'Open loop not found'; 500 on unexpected failure
items.gotchas: None beyond the join being a LEFT JOIN (loop is still returned if the parent action was deleted, with those fields null).

items.name: PATCH /api/actions/loops/{loopId}
items.purpose: Resolves or cancels an open loop via an atomic compare-and-set against status='open', preventing two operators from double-resolving the same loop.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.body.resolution: string, required when status='resolved', max 2000, redacted for secrets

items.response: { loop: updated row, security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories} }
items.errors: 400 missing/invalid status, missing resolution when resolving, or resolution over 2000 chars; 404 loop not found; 409 'Loop is already <status>' if not currently open
items.gotchas: The UPDATE's WHERE clause requires status='open'; zero affected rows triggers a follow-up SELECT to distinguish 404 (doesn't exist) from 409 (already resolved/cancelled) — this is a compare-and-set, not a blind overwrite.

items.name: GET /api/actions/stats
items.purpose: Returns 24-hour decision-throughput statistics (totals by status) plus a period-over-period change percentage.
items.auth: x-api-key or session cookie, resolved by middleware to org_id/role

inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional, scopes stats to one agent

items.response: { ...current stats fields (e.g. total, completed, failed, cancelled, approval), change_percent: number, lastUpdated: ISO string }
items.errors: 500 with a zeroed fallback stats object ('An error occurred while fetching action statistics')
items.gotchas: change_percent is computed in the route from current vs previous-period totals returned by getActionStats; 100% when previous period had zero actions but current has some.

items.name: GET /api/activity
items.purpose: Lists activity_log audit entries for the org with filtering (action, actor, resource type, time range) and pagination, plus aggregate stats (total, today, unique actors).
items.auth: Not in PUBLIC_ROUTES — standard middleware x-api-key/session auth; getOrgId(request) reads the trusted x-org-id header. All org members can read (no admin gate).

inputs.query.before: ISO-parseable timestamp, optional, filtered as created_at::timestamptz < before
inputs.query.after: ISO-parseable timestamp, optional, filtered as created_at::timestamptz > after

items.response: { events: array (activity_logs rows joined with actor name/image from users), stats: { total, today, unique_actors }, pagination: { limit, offset } }
items.errors: 400 { error: 'Invalid "before" timestamp' } / { error: 'Invalid "after" timestamp' } on unparseable dates (explicitly validated to avoid a raw Postgres 22007 surfacing as 500); 500 { error: 'Failed to fetch activity logs' }
items.gotchas: Builds a dynamic parameterized SQL WHERE clause manually (string-concatenated column/operator list, but values always bound via $n placeholders — not raw string interpolation) rather than going through a repository; created_at is stored as TEXT and compared via ::timestamptz casts on both sides per the known fresh-vs-legacy schema TEXT convention. Has its own demo-fixture route override at middle…

items.name: POST /api/admin/trigger-outcome-sweep
items.purpose: Manually triggers the lost-confirmation outcome sweep for the caller's own org (free-tier instances without cron finalize timed-out actions on demand).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin' (403 otherwise)
items.response: { ok: true, rows_swept: number, timeout_minutes: number }
items.errors: 403 Forbidden (non-admin role); 500 Sweep failed on unexpected error
items.gotchas: Timeout minutes come from org setting DASHCLAW_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (default 15, clamped 1-1440); only sweeps the caller's org, unlike the CRON_SECRET-gated org-wide /api/cron/outcome-sweep.

items.name: GET /api/identities
items.purpose: Lists registered agent public-key identities for the org.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: POST /api/identities
items.purpose: Registers (or upserts) an agent's public-key identity for signed-action verification.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')

inputs.body.public_key: required, must be a PEM-formatted public key (contains BEGIN/END PUBLIC KEY markers)

items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if agent_id/public_key missing or public_key isn't a valid PEM public key; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: public_key validation is a simple substring check (BEGIN/END PUBLIC KEY markers), not full PEM/ASN.1 parsing.

items.name: DELETE /api/identities/{agentId}
items.purpose: Revokes an agent's registered identity and expires any pending pairing requests for that agent.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 404 if identity not found; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Side effect: also expires pending pairings for the agent (expirePendingByAgent) in the same call.

items.name: GET /api/messages
items.purpose: List messages in the agent/dashboard messaging ledger, with unread counts and attached-file metadata.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.query.agent_id: optional; scopes direction/unread semantics; readerId for is_read/unread_by falls back to 'dashboard' if absent

items.errors: 500 An error occurred while fetching messages.
items.gotchas: Attachment-metadata fetch is tolerated best-effort (older installs may lack the attachments table) but logs a warning rather than failing silently. is_read for broadcast messages (to_agent_id null) is derived from parsing the read_by JSON array and checking membership of the reader id, not from a status column.

items.name: PATCH /api/messages
items.purpose: Bulk-update messages: mark a set as read (per-reader, handling both direct and broadcast semantics) or archive them.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.body.agent_id: string, optional — the reader id for 'read' action; defaults to 'dashboard'

items.response: 200: { updated } — count of messages actually updated.
items.errors: 400 message_ids array is required; 400 action must be "read" or "archive"; 500 An error occurred while updating messages.
items.gotchas: 'read' action branches per message: direct messages only count as read for the addressed to_agent_id (or 'dashboard'); broadcast messages (to_agent_id null) instead append the reader id to a read_by JSON array, and only messages where the reader wasn't already in read_by get updated/counted.

items.name: POST /api/messages
items.purpose: Send a new message (agent-to-agent, agent-to-dashboard, or broadcast) with optional file attachments, into the messaging ledger.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.body.from_agent_id: string, required — must be 'dashboard' or an existing agent in this org (403 otherwise, prevents cross-tenant spoofing)
inputs.body.to_agent_id: string, optional — if present, must be an existing agent in this org (403 otherwise); omitted = broadcast
inputs.body.message_type: string, optional, default 'info', must be one of action|info|lesson|question|status
inputs.body.subject: string, optional, max 200 chars (enforced via enforceFieldLimits)
inputs.body.body: string, required, max 2000 chars — scanned/redacted for sensitive data before storage
inputs.body.thread_id: string, optional — must be an existing open mt_* message-thread; ct_* context-thread ids are explicitly rejected with a 400
inputs.body.attachments: array, optional, max 3 items; each requires { filename, mime_type (allowlisted: png/jpeg/gif/webp/pdf/plain/markdown/csv/json), data (base64) }, max 5MB decoded per attachment, magic-byte verified ag…

items.errors: 400 Validation failed (subject/body length); 400 body is required; 400 from_agent_id is required; 403 from_agent_id/to_agent_id not found in this org; 400 message_type invalid; 400 ct_* thread rejected / Thread not found / Thread is not open; 400 at…
items.gotchas: Message body is passed through scanSensitiveData and stored redacted, not raw. Attachment binary content is verified via magic-byte signature check against the claimed mime_type (rejects mislabeled HTML/JS uploads) — text types (plain/markdown/csv) have no magic bytes and are accepted as-is, relying on Content-Disposition:attachment + nosniff on the GET side. Publishes a real-time MESSAGE_CREATED…

items.name: GET /api/messages/attachments
items.purpose: Download a single message attachment's binary content by id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: raw binary body (not JSON) with headers Content-Type: <stored mime_type>, Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<sanitized>", X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Length, Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600.
items.errors: 400 id query parameter is required; 404 Attachment not found (wrong org or nonexistent); 500 An error occurred while fetching attachment.
items.gotchas: Content-Disposition is always forced to 'attachment' (never inline) and filename is sanitized (strips quotes/CR/LF/control chars) to prevent header injection and inline HTML/script rendering at the DashClaw origin, regardless of the client's claimed mime_type.

items.name: GET /api/messages/threads
items.purpose: List message threads (mt_*) for the org, optionally filtered by status or participating agent.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.errors: 500 An error occurred while fetching threads.
items.gotchas: This is the message-thread list (mt_*), a separate table/id-space from context threads (ct_*) used elsewhere in the app — do not conflate the two.

items.name: PATCH /api/messages/threads
items.purpose: Update a message thread's status and/or summary (e.g. resolving a thread).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.body.status: string, optional — defaults to existing status if omitted
inputs.body.summary: string, optional — defaults to existing summary if omitted

items.errors: 400 thread_id is required; 400 thread_id must be a message-thread id (mt_*) — rejects ct_* ids with a pointer to /api/context/threads; 404 Thread not found; 500 An error occurred while updating thread.
items.gotchas: resolved_at is only stamped the first time status transitions into 'resolved' (existing.status !== 'resolved') — re-PATCHing an already-resolved thread doesn't overwrite resolved_at.

items.name: POST /api/messages/threads
items.purpose: Create a new message thread (mt_*) with a name and participant list.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.body.name: string, required
inputs.body.participants: optional, JSON-serialized as-is into message_threads.participants (conventionally an array of agent ids); no shape enforcement

items.errors: 400 name is required; 400 created_by is required; 500 An error occurred while creating thread.
items.gotchas: Thread id is generated as `mt_` + 24-char hex (no dashes) — always distinguishable from a context-thread `ct_` id. Insert is idempotent on the generated id via ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING (retry-safe).

items.name: GET /api/messages/threads/{threadId}
items.purpose: Fetch a single message thread by id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.errors: 400 Valid thread_id required (missing or not mt_*-prefixed); 404 Thread not found; 500 An error occurred while fetching thread.
items.gotchas: Same mt_*-prefix validation as the collection route's PATCH — a ct_* id here 400s rather than silently returning a wrong/empty result.

items.name: GET /api/sessions
items.purpose: Lists agent coding sessions (agent_sessions) for the org, filterable by agent_id/status.
items.auth: x-api-key

inputs.query.limit: string, optional (parsed/clamped in lib, default 50 max 200)

items.errors: 500 { error: 'Failed to list sessions' }
items.gotchas: None beyond standard org-scoping.

items.name: POST /api/sessions
items.purpose: Creates a new agent coding session, starting status 'running', and records an initial session_event (seq 1, kind 'running').
items.auth: x-api-key
items.errors: 400 { error: 'agent_id is required' }; 500 { error: 'Failed to create session' }
items.gotchas: id is generated as 'sess_' + 12-char hex (from randomUUID, hyphens stripped); creates a row in a separate session_events table as a side effect of session creation, not just agent_sessions.

items.name: GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}
items.purpose: Fetch a single session with aggregated action_count/last_action_at/total_cost.
items.auth: x-api-key
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Session not found' }; 500 { error: 'Failed to fetch session' }
items.gotchas: None beyond org-scoping.

items.name: PATCH /api/sessions/{sessionId}
items.purpose: Updates session lifecycle state (status/green_level/branch_freshness/commits_behind/blocked_reason) and/or attaches a closing summary; used by the MCP dashclaw_session_end tool.
items.auth: x-api-key

inputs.body.commits_behind: number, optional (checked with == null so 0 counts as present)
inputs.body.summary: string, optional — only recorded if a status transition also occurs

items.errors: 400 { error: 'No update fields provided' } if status/green_level/branch_freshness/commits_behind/blocked_reason are all absent; 409 { error: 'Session is closed and cannot be updated' } if the session exists but is already terminal; 404 { error: 'Ses…
items.gotchas: summary alone (no status) fails the initial field-presence check and is silently dropped — there is no terminal session_event to attach it to without a status transition (documented in-code). A closed session returns 409, not 404, disambiguated by a follow-up getSession call.

items.name: GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/actions
items.purpose: Paginated list of action_records attributed to this session.
items.auth: x-api-key
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Session not found' }; 500 { error: 'Failed to fetch session actions' }
items.gotchas: Shares the exact match predicate with the session's action_count aggregate (per in-code comment) so total here always equals the session detail's action_count card.

items.name: GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/events
items.purpose: Lists lifecycle session_events (status transitions) for a session.
items.auth: x-api-key
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Session not found' }; 500 { error: 'Failed to fetch session events' }
items.gotchas: Bounded read (in-code comment notes events are normally few — one per status transition — but a PATCH loop could grow the table; the query has a defensive limit).

items.name: GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/retro

items.name: DELETE /api/keys
items.purpose: Revoke (soft-delete) an API key by id (admin only).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin' — 403 otherwise.
items.errors: 400 Valid key id is required; 403 Admin access required; 404 API key not found (wrong org or nonexistent); 409 API key is already revoked; 500 Failed to revoke API key.
items.gotchas: Revocation sets revoked_at in the DB immediately, but middleware caches resolved API keys in-memory per-instance for up to 5 minutes (API_KEY_CACHE_TTL) — a just-revoked key can still authenticate against a warm serverless instance for up to that window; this route cannot invalidate that cache (different runtime). Fire-and-forget meter decrement after revoke.

items.name: GET /api/keys
items.purpose: List the org's API keys (metadata only, never raw key values).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate on GET.
items.response: 200: { keys: [{ id, key_prefix, label, role, last_used_at, created_at, revoked_at }] }.
items.errors: 500 Failed to fetch API keys.
items.gotchas: On a fresh self-host install before migration (Postgres error 42P01, table not found) AND isSelfHostModeEnabled(), returns { keys: [] } instead of erroring so the dashboard doesn't crash pre-migration.

items.name: POST /api/keys
items.purpose: Generate a new API key for the org (admin only), returning the raw key value exactly once.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin' — 403 otherwise.

inputs.body.label: string, optional, default 'API Key', max 256 chars
inputs.body.role: string, optional, default 'member', must be one of API_KEY_ROLES ('admin'|'member') — defaults to 'member' specifically so agent keys are never accidentally admin

items.response: 201: { key: { id, raw_key, prefix, label, role, storageWarning } }. raw_key is shown only in this response and can never be retrieved again (stored as SHA-256 hash).
items.errors: 400 Label must be a string of 256 characters or fewer; 400 role must be one of: admin, member; 402 { error, code: 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED', usage, limit } when the org's api_keys quota is exceeded; 403 Admin access required; 500 Failed to generate API key.
items.gotchas: Quota-checked against the org plan before insert (checkQuotaFast). Fire-and-forget meter increment after insert. key_prefix stores 16 chars (8 unique hex digits after the fixed 'oc_live_' prefix) to let the dashboard visually distinguish keys without exposing the full value.

items.name: GET /api/keys/reveal
items.purpose: Return the operator's bootstrap API key (DASHCLAW_API_KEY env var) so a signed-in admin doesn't have to hunt for it in .env.local or Vercel deploy output. Powers Mission Control QuickStart and the /settings Environment reveal button.
items.auth: Requires x-user-id from middleware (NextAuth/local-admin cookie session only — never API-key or dev-mode fallback traffic) AND getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'. Additionally denies hosted-trial princi…
items.errors: 401 Authentication required (no x-user-id); 403 Admin access required (non-admin org role); 403 trial-principal denial (from denyTrialPrincipal, hosted-only); 404 { error, hint } when DASHCLAW_API_KEY is not configured on this instance.
items.gotchas: Does NOT query the api_keys table — those workspace-generated keys are SHA-256 hashed and permanently unrecoverable by design; this route only ever returns the single operator bootstrap key from the environment. On self-host (no trial principals) the trial-denial check is a no-op.

items.name: POST /api/approvals/bulk
items.purpose: Admin-only bulk allow/deny resolution for a flood of pending approvals matching a policy's compiled action_types (last 24h), used by the approval-flood banner.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin'; requires an attributable userId (getUserId)
items.response: { resolved: number, failed: number, matched: number }
items.errors: 403 Admin access required / APPROVER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED (no attributable principal); 400 invalid decision, missing filter.policy_id, protected_path policy type, or policy has no action_types; 404 Policy not found
items.gotchas: Webhooks are intentionally skipped in bulk (avoids destination stampede) — resolution recorded only via audit log. protected_path policies are rejected; resolve those from /approvals individually. Sweeps expired approvals first so dead rows aren't resolved.

items.name: GET /api/approvals/floods
items.purpose: Returns current interruption-budget (approval flood) state per-policy and fleet-wide; re-evaluates and persists trip/clear transitions on every read.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.query.include_synthetic: '1', ephemeral would-trip view counting synthetic/smoke traffic too, nothing persisted/notified

items.response: { floods: [{policy_id, name, count, tripped_at}], fleet: {tripped_at,count}|null, budget: {...}, synthetic_included?: true }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error on failure
items.gotchas: This GET has a write side-effect — it persists flood trip/clear transitions on every call; that's also the only mechanism by which a flood clears (no scheduler).

items.name: POST /api/approvals/{actionId}
items.purpose: Human-in-the-loop approval/denial of a pending_approval action; updates status, fires webhooks/notifications, and reconciles x402 purchases on deny.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin'; requires attributable userId

inputs.body.reasoning: string, optional (redacted for secrets before storage)

items.response: { success: true, action: {...}, security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories} }
items.errors: 403 Admin access required / APPROVER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED / SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN (creator approving own action, unless userId==='operator'); 404 Action not found; 400 invalid decision or action not pending_approval; 409 already resolved by another a…
items.gotchas: Lazily expires overdue pending approvals on read (self-healing) before processing; a denied x402_purchase action is reconciled to release reserved spend; clears external (Discord/Telegram) approval-request notifications via next/server `after()`.

items.name: GET /api/artifacts
items.purpose: Lists artifacts for the org with optional filters.

items.name: POST /api/artifacts

items.errors: 400 artifact_type and name are required; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise

items.name: POST /api/artifacts/evidence-bundle
items.purpose: Builds an evidence bundle for a given action (decision trail + supporting data) and, by default, persists it as an artifact.

inputs.body.persist: bool, optional, default true (false skips persistence)

items.response: Evidence bundle object (bundle.action includes declared_goal/action_id/agent_id) returned directly
items.errors: 400 action_id is required; 404 action_not_found; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: When persisted, the created artifact is tagged ['evidence-bundle', 'auto-generated'] and named from the action's declared_goal or id.

items.purpose: Fetches a single artifact by id.

items.purpose: Deletes an artifact by id.

items.name: GET /api/assumptions

items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { assumptions: [...], total: number, drift_summary?: {total, at_risk, validated, invalidated, unvalidated}, lastUpdated: ISOString }
items.errors: 500 on fetch failure (returns assumptions: [])
items.gotchas: drift_score: 0 for validated, null for invalidated, else 0-100 scaled by age over 30 days; drift_summary comes from a separate whole-table aggregate query (not derived from the returned page) so it stays correct once the table exceeds the page limit.

items.name: POST /api/assumptions
items.purpose: Creates a new assumption tied to a parent action.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body: validated by validateAssumption(); fields include assumption, basis, invalidated_reason, action_id (required, must reference an existing action), assumption_id (optional, server-generates asm_<uuid> …

items.response: { assumption: {...}, assumption_id: string, security: {clean, findings_count, critical_count, categories} } (201)
items.errors: 400 Invalid JSON body / Validation failed (details from validateAssumption); 404 Parent action not found; 409 duplicate assumption_id; 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: assumption/basis/invalidated_reason are redacted for secrets (redactAny) before storage.

items.name: GET /api/assumptions/{assumptionId}
items.purpose: Fetches a single assumption by id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.errors: 404 Assumption not found; 500 on fetch failure

items.name: PATCH /api/assumptions/{assumptionId}
items.purpose: Validates or invalidates an assumption; on invalidation, notifies the owning agent.

items.response: { assumption: {...} } for validate; { assumption: {...}, security: {...}, notification?: {message_id}, notification_error?: 'notification_failed' } for invalidate
items.errors: 400 validated must be boolean / invalidated_reason required or too long; 404 Assumption not found; 409 Assumption is already invalidated (incl. race loss on compare-and-set); 500 Internal server error

items.name: GET /api/auth/config
items.purpose: Returns which OAuth/local-auth methods are configured, for the login UI to render available sign-in options (and whether any sign-in method is configured at all).
items.auth: Public — /api/auth is in PUBLIC_ROUTES (prefix match, boundary-aware) so this bypasses middleware entirely; the handler itself performs no auth check (purely informational, no secrets returned).
items.response: { isProd: boolean, providers: [{ id, name }], localAuthEnabled: boolean, message: string|null }
items.errors: None — no try/catch, no explicit error paths beyond default framework 500 on unexpected throw
items.gotchas: In non-production (NODE_ENV !== 'production'), injects mock GitHub/Google provider entries ('GitHub (Mock)'/'Google (Mock)') if the real ones aren't configured, so local dev always shows OAuth buttons even without real OAuth app credentials configured.

items.name: DELETE /api/auth/local
items.purpose: Logs out of the local admin session by clearing the dashclaw-local-session cookie.
items.auth: Public — under /api/auth prefix. No auth check at all in the handler (clearing a cookie is safe to allow from any caller state).
items.response: { ok: true } with Set-Cookie: dashclaw-local-session=; maxAge=0 (clears cookie)
items.errors: None — unconditional success
items.gotchas: No error handling/try-catch; always returns 200 regardless of whether a session cookie existed.

items.name: POST /api/auth/local
items.purpose: Local admin password login: verifies a submitted password against DASHCLAW_LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD (self-host mode), applies brute-force lockout, and on success sets an HttpOnly session cookie (JWT) for the local-admin identity.
items.auth: Public — under /api/auth prefix, bypasses middleware. Self-guards entirely on the env password: 404 if DASHCLAW_LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD isn't set (feature disabled), otherwise timing-safe compare (lengt…
items.response: { ok: true } with Set-Cookie: dashclaw-local-session=<JWT>, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 7-day maxAge, Secure flag follows scheme (NEXTAUTH_URL startsWith https) not NODE_ENV
items.errors: 404 (empty body) if local admin password feature disabled; 401 { error: 'Password is required.' } if body has no password; 401 { error: 'Incorrect password.' } on mismatch (with a lockout-triggering failure record + 500ms delay); 429 { error: 'Too m…
items.gotchas: Login-lockout store failures are fail-open by design (comment: 'the env password is the authentication; if the guard store is unreachable... let login proceed rather than locking the operator out') — lockout is best-effort, not a hard security boundary. JWT is signed HS256 with NEXTAUTH_SECRET, claims include sub='local-admin', userId='usr_local_admin', orgId=DASHCLAW_API_KEY_ORG (default org_def…

items.name: GET /api/behavior/insights
items.purpose: Returns the latest safe aggregate behavior snapshot for the org (used by hosted Policy Coach 'learning in background' panel).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { snapshot: Snapshot|null } where Snapshot = {schema_version, pushed_at, host_label, window_days, sample_count, agent_count, oldest_ts, newest_ts, signals:{destructive_commands,protected_path_writes,failed_actions,high_risk_actions,blocked,approvals}, agents:[{agent_id,count,destructive,protected_writes,failed,tools}]}
items.errors: 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: Stored as a JSON string under settings key BEHAVIOR_INSIGHTS_SNAPSHOT.

items.name: POST /api/behavior/insights
items.purpose: Accepts a machine-pushed safe aggregate behavior snapshot; rebuilds it field-by-field from an allowlist so no raw behavior data can leak through.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body: Snapshot-shaped object (see GET response); only allowlisted fields are read, everything else ignored

items.response: { ok: true, pushed_at: ISOString } or { skipped: true, reason: 'stale' }
items.errors: 400 Invalid body / Empty or invalid snapshot; 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: Monotonic guard: rejects (skips) an incoming snapshot whose newest_ts is provably older than the stored one, so multi-machine pushes for one org can't clobber a newer snapshot with a stale one. Value serialized with an agent-list trim loop to stay under the settings 10000-char value cap (VALUE_CAP=9500).

items.name: GET /api/behavior/recorder
items.purpose: Returns current behavior-recorder config for the org (polled by the local agent hook to decide whether to capture samples).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { enabled: boolean, until: string|null, effective: boolean, upload_enabled: boolean }
items.errors: 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: effective = enabled && not expired (until, if set, is an auto-stop timestamp).

items.name: POST /api/behavior/recorder
items.purpose: Admin sets recorder enablement, optional auto-stop window, and the anonymized-sample-upload opt-in flag.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin'

inputs.body.duration_days: number, optional (>0 sets auto-stop window; null/0/omitted = until turned off)
inputs.body.upload_enabled: boolean, optional (only written when explicitly boolean)

items.errors: 403 Admin access required; 400 Invalid setting key/category (from repository validation); 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: upload_enabled defaults to false and is only mutated when the body explicitly sends a boolean — omitting it leaves the existing value untouched.

items.name: GET /api/behavior/samples
items.purpose: Returns behavior-sample status/counts for the Policy Coach, preferring local machine-global samples and falling back to org-scoped uploaded samples; with ?list=N returns recent redacted sample records.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.query.list: int, optional, 1-200; when present returns recent samples instead of status

items.response: Without list: {sample_count, agent_count, agents:[{agent_id,count}], oldest_ts, newest_ts, by_day?, ready, min_samples, sample_source:'local'|'uploaded', recorder_enabled?, remote?, dir?}. With list: {samples:[...], count, sample_source}
items.errors: 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: sample_source distinguishes whether data came from the local filesystem sample store (machine-global, no org axis) or this org's uploaded/ingested samples table.

items.name: POST /api/behavior/samples/ingest
items.purpose: Opt-in ingestion of anonymized behavior samples uploaded from an agent's machine; server rebuilds every row field-by-field from an allowlist and re-redacts, then prunes retention.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; additionally gated on org setting BEHAVIOR_UPLOAD_ENABLED=true

inputs.body.samples: array, required, non-empty, max 500 per batch (~1MB body cap); each sample: event_id, agent_id, ts (required identity fields) plus session_hash (sh_ hash), tool, tool_category, action_type, command_s…

items.errors: 413 Payload too large; 400 Invalid body / not { samples: [...] } / samples empty or exceeds MAX_BATCH / no valid samples in batch; 403 Behavior sample upload is not enabled for this org; 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: read_path_hashes/write_path_hashes MUST match ph_[0-9a-f]{12} and session_hash sh_[0-9a-f]{12} — raw (unhashed) paths are silently dropped, never persisted under the hash columns.

items.name: POST /api/behavior/simulate
items.purpose: Replays a behavior suggestion or an edited rule against recorded samples, returning decision counts (allow/warn/require_approval/block) and likely false positives, backing the mandatory simulate-before-adopt review.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.rule: object, optional (preview an edited/custom rule; requires rule.kind); at least one of suggestion_id/rule required

items.response: { suggestion_id: string|null, rule: {...}, simulation: {...decision counts + false positives...}, sample_source: 'local'|'uploaded' }
items.errors: 400 suggestion_id or rule is required / rule.kind is required; 404 Suggestion not found; 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: Simulation is scoped to the rule's agent_id when set.

items.name: GET /api/behavior/suggestions
items.purpose: Analyzes behavior samples into per-agent envelopes and evidence-backed policy suggestions, honoring dismiss suppression.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { agents: [...], suggestions: [...], dismissed: [...], sample_count: number, sample_source: 'local'|'uploaded' }
items.errors: 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: Deterministic analysis; prefers local samples, falls back to org-scoped uploaded samples.

items.name: POST /api/behavior/suggestions
items.purpose: Acts on a behavior suggestion: dismiss, adopt (create an INACTIVE guard-policy draft or record an accepted advisory), or undo a prior dismiss/adopt.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.edited: object, optional (adopt — only EDITABLE_RULE_KEYS: action, risk_threshold, paths, max_reloads, window_minutes, max_failures, min_tier)

items.response: dismiss: {dismissed:true, record}; adopt (advisory): {adopted:true, advisory:true, simulation, note}; adopt (enforceable): {adopted:true, advisory:false, policy, simulation, note}; undo: {ok:true, suggestion_id, removed:true, policy_kept}
items.errors: 400 suggestion_id required / Simulation review required before adopting / No samples to simulate against / Suggestion is not enforceable / Invalid policy / Invalid action; 404 Suggestion not found / Nothing recorded to undo
items.gotchas: Adopting an enforceable suggestion always creates the guard policy with active=0 (never auto-enforced) plus a status='adopted' suppression row so it stops re-surfacing; undo keeps the created draft policy (only removes the suppression record) and echoes policy_kept.

items.name: POST /api/billing/checkout

items.errors: 501 BILLING_NOT_CONFIGURED (no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) / PRICE_NOT_CONFIGURED; 400 INVALID_PLAN; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: Plan-to-Stripe-price mapping comes from env vars STRIPE_PRICE_PRO / STRIPE_PRICE_BUSINESS; stripe_customer_id is persisted on the organizations row via a direct SQL UPDATE (only direct-SQL usage in this route, not through a repository).

items.name: GET /api/billing/portal
items.purpose: Creates a Stripe Billing Portal session for the org's existing Stripe customer.

items.gotchas: Requires the org to have already checked out once (customerId comes from getOrgStripeCustomerId).

items.name: GET /api/calibration/controller
items.purpose: Snapshot of the calibrated interruption controller (theory: docs/architecture/governance-core-theory.md §1, UI: /calibration): settings (mode, target rate α), calibrated state (θ, labeled benign/denied counts, long-run + windowed observed false-interruption rate), top per-agent e-process alarms, recent adjudication events, and the org's active risk_threshold policies for θ-vs-policy context.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { settings:{mode, target_rate}, state:{theta, labeled_total, labeled_benign, labeled_denied, loss_sum, observed_rate, observed_window_rate, observed_window}, defaults:{gamma, alarm_at, p0, theta_floor}, alarms:[{agent_id, e, n, denied, alarmed_at}] (top 25 by e), events (last 200), risk_threshold_policies:[{id, name, threshold, action}] sorted by threshold }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error
items.gotchas: observed_window_rate is computed over the most recent 50 adjudications for display; state falls back to a fresh zeroed calibration state when the org has none yet, so the route never 404s.

items.name: POST /api/calibration/controller
items.purpose: Admin-only controller controls: set mode ('off'|'shadow'|'active'), set the target false-interruption rate α, reset a single agent's e-process alarm, or reset the whole calibrated state. Activating the controller is a human policy decision made here by click (MAINTAINER.md §3); the controller itself only ever tightens.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin'
items.response: { success:true, changes:{...} } echoing exactly the fields that changed
items.errors: 403 Admin access required; 400 invalid mode / target_rate out of 0.01-0.5 / empty body (Nothing to change); 404 No calibration entry for that agent (reset_agent_alarm)
items.gotchas: Mode/target live in the settings table and the guard hot path reads them via a 30s-TTL cached settings read — the route invalidates this instance's guard settings + calibration caches immediately, but other instances converge within ≤30s. Every change is audit-logged as calibration.controller_updated.

items.name: GET /api/calibration/proposals
items.purpose: Computes calibration-vector proposals on read from the org's decision ledger + uploaded samples (same pipeline as the weekly miner), joined with any persisted human ratify/dismiss/forge decisions.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { window_days, inputs:{decisions, decisions_truncated_at_limit, uploaded_samples, synthetic_excluded}, proposals:[{...mined fields, representative, status, decision}], counts:{pending,ratified,dismissed,forged} }
items.errors: 400 invalid status value; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: Synthetic (smoke-marked) events are always filtered out; representative payloads are redacted for secrets; ratified-but-not-yet-forged decisions whose shape no longer mines in the current window are synthesized from their stored snapshot (from_snapshot:true) rather than silently dropped.

items.name: POST /api/calibration/proposals
items.purpose: Records an admin's judgment on a calibration proposal: ratify, dismiss, undo, or mark_forged (maintainer closes the loop after adding a real calibration vector).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin'

inputs.body.proposal: object snapshot, required for ratify/dismiss (rule, suggested_label, suggested_name kebab-case, provenance, ratify_command?, representative?)
inputs.body.vector_name: string, required for mark_forged, kebab-case max 64 chars

items.response: ratify/dismiss: {ok:true, proposal_id, decision}; undo: {ok:true, proposal_id, removed:true}; mark_forged: {ok:true, proposal_id, forged:true}
items.errors: 403 Admin access required; 400 invalid action / proposal_id format / snapshot shape errors / missing or oversized reason / invalid vector_name; 404 No decision recorded for this proposal (undo/mark_forged); 409 Only a ratified proposal can be marked…
items.gotchas: Snapshot is validated by shape only, not recomputed against the live mine (admin judgment ledger, precedent from tuning dismissals); dismiss reason and representative are redacted for secrets before storage.

items.name: GET /api/capabilities
items.purpose: Lists capabilities for the org with category/risk_level/search filters.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error on failure

items.name: POST /api/capabilities
items.purpose: Creates a new capability.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.name: string, required
inputs.body.slug: string, optional (slugified from name if absent)
inputs.body.risk_level: string, optional, must be a valid RISK_LEVELS value
inputs.body.source_type: string, optional, must be a valid SOURCE_TYPES value

items.errors: 400 name is required / invalid risk_level or source_type / invalid invocation_schema; 409 A capability with this slug already exists; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise

items.name: GET /api/capabilities/health
items.purpose: Lists capability health summaries (status, certification, staleness) with filters, used for the capability health dashboard.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error on failure

items.name: GET /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}
items.purpose: Fetches a single capability by id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.errors: 404 Capability not found; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise

items.name: PATCH /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}
items.purpose: Updates a capability's fields.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.invocation_schema: object, optional (re-validated when it or source_type changes)
inputs.body....other capability fields: merged via COALESCE against current row

items.errors: 404 Capability not found; 400 invalid risk_level/source_type/invocation_schema; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: Update reads current values via SQL COALESCE at UPDATE time (not merged from the earlier SELECT) so two concurrent PATCHes don't clobber each other's non-overlapping fields.

items.name: DELETE /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}
items.purpose: Deletes a capability.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.errors: 404 Capability not found; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise

items.name: GET /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/access
items.purpose: Lists access rules (agent-specific and org-wide default) for a capability.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { rules: [{rule_id, org_id, capability_id, agent_id, access, reason, created_by, created_at}] }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error on failure
items.gotchas: Rules ordered org-wide-default-first (agent_id IS NULL ASC), then by created_at DESC.

items.name: POST /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/access
items.purpose: Creates a new access rule (agent-specific or org-wide default) for a capability.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.created_by: read from x-user-id header, not body

items.errors: 400 access level is required / Invalid access level / rule already exists (duplicate agent+capability or default); apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: Only one org-wide default rule and one per-agent rule per capability are allowed (enforced by partial unique DB indexes, caught as 23505 unique_violation and surfaced as 400 'already exists').

items.name: GET /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/access/check
items.purpose: Evaluates effective access for a given agent on a capability (agent-specific rule wins over org-wide default; default access is 'allow' if no rules exist).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware (org-authenticated preview surface)

inputs.query.verified: 'true' previews what a JWT-verified identity would get; default false

items.response: AccessEvaluation object (effective access decision + matching rule details) returned directly from evaluateAccess
items.errors: 400 agent_id query param is required; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: verified is a preview-only query param on this route — real enforcement routes resolve verified from the actual JWT, never from a query param.

items.name: DELETE /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/access/{ruleId}
items.purpose: Deletes a specific access rule by id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.errors: 404 rule_not_found; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: capabilityId is part of the URL but the DELETE only scopes by orgId + ruleId.

items.name: GET /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/health
items.purpose: Returns a capability's current health/circuit-breaker status merged with its capability record.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via middleware authenticateProtectedApi; also accepts operator key, same-origin session, or OAuth bearer)
items.response: capability + health object from getCapabilityWithHealth() (fields not enumerated in this route file)
items.errors: 404 'Capability not found'; 500 via apiErrorResponse (code CAPABILITY_HEALTH)
items.gotchas: Health/circuit-breaker state is updated as a side effect of invoke/test calls, not computed live here.

items.name: GET /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/history
items.purpose: Returns paginated invocation/test history for one capability.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: object returned by getCapabilityHistory() (fields not enumerated in this route file)
items.errors: 404 'Capability not found'; 500 via apiErrorResponse (code CAPABILITY_HISTORY)
items.gotchas: capability is bridged from a loose Record<string,unknown> DB row into { capability_id, name, slug } for the history lookup.

items.name: POST /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/invoke
items.purpose: Executes a governed real HTTP call to an http_api capability: runs guard, DLP scan, quota, circuit-breaker and access-control checks, then invokes the endpoint and records the outcome.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi); agent identity additionally resolved via resolveAgentIdentity (JWKS-verified JWT sub overrides body.agent_id, else self-asserted/unverified)

inputs.body.agent_id: optional, overridden by verified JWT sub
remaining body fields are forwarded to the capability endpoint per its schema

items.response: { success:true, action_id, result, elapsed_ms, governed:true, retry_metadata?, quota_warning?, security:{clean,findings_count,critical_count,categories} }
items.errors: 404 capability_not_found; 400 not_invocable/auth_not_configured/endpoint_not_configured/capability_contract_invalid/capability_input_invalid; 403 blocked_by_policy or access_denied; 202 pending_approval; 402 quota_exceeded; 503 circuit_breaker_open;…
items.gotchas: Creates action_records rows for every path (blocked/pending_approval/running/completed/failed); DLP-redacts a 500-char input summary; fires operator approval notifications (Telegram/Discord/webhook) on require_approval; updates capability health_status fire-and-forget after the call so checkCircuitBreaker can count consecutive failures; meters capability_invocations + governed_actions on success …

items.name: POST /api/capabilities/{capabilityId}/test
items.purpose: Fires the same real capability call as invoke (for connectivity/health testing) but still runs it through guard first, and updates health_status/certification_status from the result.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

remaining body fields forwarded to the capability endpoint

items.response: { success, tested, capability_id, test_action_id, result|error/message, elapsed_ms, health_status, certification_status, retry_metadata? }
items.errors: 404 capability_not_found; 400 not_invocable/auth_not_configured/endpoint_not_configured/capability_contract_invalid/capability_input_invalid; 403 blocked_by_policy; 202 pending_approval; 504 capability_timeout; 502 other execution failure
items.gotchas: Deliberately mirrors invoke's guard gating (block/require_approval) because a 'test' still hits the org's real credentials/endpoint; unlike invoke it does NOT run the quota, circuit-breaker, or access-control checks; risk_score for guard is hardcoded to 5.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/alerts
items.purpose: Lists code-session alerts for the org, optionally filtered to unread only, plus the unread count.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: none explicit (no try/catch in this route)
items.gotchas: No pagination offset param, only limit.

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/alerts/read-all
items.purpose: Marks code-session alerts as read, either specific ids or all.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

inputs.body.ids: optional number[]; non-numeric entries filtered out

items.errors: none explicit; malformed/empty JSON body is tolerated (treated as {})
items.gotchas: Omitting ids (or passing a non-array) marks per markAlertsRead's null semantics — check the repository if 'mark all' vs 'no-op' matters.

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/ingest-jsonl
items.purpose: Bulk-ingests a Claude Code JSONL transcript (or gzip/brotli-compressed envelope), parses it into a session + messages + tool-uses, and computes signals/alerts.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

inputs.body.session_uuid: optional, must match parsed sessionId if present
inputs.headers.x-dashclaw-encoding: 'br'|'gzip' — flags a compressed raw body (current CLI wire transport)

items.errors: 413 gzip_body_too_large_after_decode / compressed_jsonl_too_large_after_decode / jsonl_lines_too_large; 400 invalid_json / gzip_body_decode_failed / invalid_source_host / missing_jsonl_lines / compressed_jsonl_decode_failed / no_session_uuid_in_json…
items.gotchas: MAX_LINES=200,000; MAX_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES=50MB; the signals/alerts computation step is wrapped in try/catch and failures there are only logged, not surfaced (ingest still succeeds with 0 signals/alerts).

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/ingest-live
items.purpose: Per-turn incremental ingest for hook-based agents (e.g. Hermes) that don't dump a full JSONL transcript; appends one turn or, with finalize:true, runs the optimizer+alerts pass on the completed session.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

inputs.body.tool_calls: optional array, max 64, each { name, tool_use_id?, target? }
inputs.body.ended_at / completed / interrupted: finalize-only fields (not otherwise consumed in this route)

items.response: append: { project, session:{id,session_uuid,turn_index,inserted_tool_uses}, agent_id }; finalize: { project, session:{session_uuid,finalized:true,found,signals_inserted,alerts_inserted,stuck_loops}, agent_id }
items.errors: 400 invalid_json / invalid_body / invalid_source_host / missing_session_uuid; 413 too_many_tool_calls / preview_too_large
items.gotchas: finalize failures are swallowed and logged (returns found:false) so the hook never gets stuck retrying; MAX_BODY_BYTES=64KB, MAX_TOOL_CALLS=64.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/manifests/{manifestId}
items.purpose: Fetches a previously saved optimal-files write manifest (TTL-bound) for the CLI to apply.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: { id, session_id, project_cwd, plan, expires_at, created_at }
items.errors: 404 not_found_or_expired
items.gotchas: Manifest is created by POST .../optimal-files/manifest and expires after 24h.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/memos
items.purpose: Lists saved weekly memos for a project.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 400 missing_project; 404 project_not_found
items.gotchas: Accepts either the project id or its slug; slug lookups scan the full listProjects() result.

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/memos/regenerate
items.purpose: Regenerates the current-week memo for a project from the last 7 days of sessions (and prior 7 for comparison).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 400 missing_project; 404 project_not_found
items.gotchas: No request body is read; the window is fixed at 7/14 days server-side.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/projects
items.purpose: Lists all code-session projects for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: none explicit
items.gotchas: none beyond DELETE below

items.name: DELETE /api/code-sessions/projects
items.purpose: Clears every code session and project for the org (org-wide wipe of code-session telemetry).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

inputs.query.confirm: must equal 'all' or request is rejected

items.errors: 400 confirm_required (hint: pass ?confirm=all)
items.gotchas: Irreversible; deletes sessions first (project_id has no cascade); handoff bundles survive via SET NULL.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/projects/{projectId}
items.purpose: Fetches one project's record.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: none

items.name: DELETE /api/code-sessions/projects/{projectId}
items.purpose: Deletes one project and all its sessions.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: Irreversible; sessions are deleted first (project_id has no cascade); handoff bundles survive via SET NULL.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/projects/{projectId}/sessions
items.purpose: Lists code sessions belonging to a project.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: none explicit (no not-found check on the project itself here)
items.gotchas: Does not validate that projectId exists — an unknown id simply returns an empty sessions array.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}
items.purpose: Fetches full detail for one code session (session row + messages + tool-uses).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: getSessionDetail() result: { session, messages, toolUses } (per usage in sibling routes)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: none

items.name: DELETE /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}
items.purpose: Deletes one code session.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: Irreversible; message/tool-use/signal children cascade via the 0006 FKs.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}/autopsy
items.purpose: Builds a structured post-mortem ('autopsy') of a session from its detail record.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: object returned by buildAutopsyFromDetail() (fields not enumerated in this route file)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: none

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}/insights
items.purpose: Returns detected repeated tool-call runs plus stored optimizer signals for a session.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: repeated_runs is recomputed live via detectRepeatedRuns() on each call, not read from storage.

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}/optimal-files/manifest
items.purpose: Builds and persists (24h TTL) a file-write manifest from caller-selected optimal-files bundle entries, for the CLI to apply to disk.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

inputs.body.selections: array (required), each { path: string, content?: string }

items.errors: 400 invalid_json / missing_selections / invalid_path / path_not_in_bundle; 404 not_found (session)
items.gotchas: Path allowlist restricted to CLAUDE.md, .claude/dashclaw/, .claude/agentlens/ (legacy prefix, kept for old-client manifests), .claude/rules/, .claude/hooks/, .claude/skills/; rejects '..' path traversal; server does NOT re-run the secret scan on caller-supplied content overrides (the CLI does at apply time).

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}/optimal-files/merge-preview
items.purpose: Previews how one candidate optimal-files entry would merge into an existing file at a given path.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: object returned by previewBundleMerge() (fields not enumerated in this route file)
items.errors: 400 invalid_json / missing_path; 404 not_found
items.gotchas: The server cannot read the caller's filesystem — existingContent is always passed as null, so the plan reflects a 'no existing content supplied' preview; the real on-disk merge happens client-side at apply time.

items.name: POST /api/code-sessions/sessions/{sessionId}/optimal-files/preview
items.purpose: Builds and returns the full optimal-files candidate bundle for a session (CLAUDE.md / .claude/* suggestions) without persisting a manifest.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 not_found
items.gotchas: projectFiles/existingPaths are always null (server has no filesystem access), so overwrite_risk on every entry is 'unknown'.

items.name: GET /api/code-sessions/subagent-roi
items.purpose: Computes subagent tool-use attribution ROI (cost/savings) from stored code-session data.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: none explicit
items.gotchas: Raw SQL lives in the repository (listSubagentToolUseAttribution) per the route-level no-direct-SQL guardrail; ROI math (computeRoiFromRows) is shared with the project-page UI.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/evidence
items.purpose: Pulls live guard-decision + action-record enforcement evidence for compliance reporting.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: { window, window_days, evidence:{guard_decisions_total, guard_decisions_blocked, approval_requests, action_records_total, breakdown, action_breakdown}, generated_at }
items.errors: 500 'Internal server error'
items.gotchas: approval_requests counts both require_approval AND warn decisions together.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/exports
items.purpose: Lists compliance export records for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 'Failed to fetch exports'
items.gotchas: none

items.name: POST /api/compliance/exports
items.purpose: Creates a compliance export record and synchronously generates a signed, hash-chained export bundle covering one or more frameworks.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: 201 with the created export record (generation runs inline before responding; a generation failure still returns 201 with the record left in 'failed' status by generateExport)
items.errors: 400 'frameworks array is required'; 500 'Failed to create export'
items.gotchas: report_content is a signed JSON bundle (Ed25519/JWKS via app/lib/integrity), hash-chained to the previous completed export for tamper-evidence — no longer plain markdown/JSON; each POST also writes a compliance_snapshots row per framework.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/exports/{exportId}
items.purpose: Fetches one export record, including its report_content bundle.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 'Export not found'; 500 'Failed to fetch export'
items.gotchas: none

items.name: DELETE /api/compliance/exports/{exportId}
items.purpose: Deletes an export record.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 'Failed to delete export'
items.gotchas: No existence check — DELETE on a non-existent id still returns { deleted: true }.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/exports/{exportId}/download
items.purpose: Streams a completed compliance export's signed bundle as a downloadable .dcbundle.json attachment.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: raw report_content bytes (application/json) with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename '<name>_<completed date>.dcbundle.json'
items.errors: 404 'Export not found'; 409 'Export not ready' (status !== 'completed'); 500 'Failed to download export'
items.gotchas: report_content is now a signed hash-chained bundle, not raw markdown/JSON; independently re-verifiable via POST /api/integrity/verify or GET /.well-known/jwks.json — the human-readable report lives at bundle.payload.report.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/frameworks
items.purpose: Lists available compliance frameworks (SOC2, ISO27001, NIST AI RMF, etc.) with control counts.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 'Internal server error'
items.gotchas: Frameworks are static bundled definitions (listFrameworks/loadFramework), not org data.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/gaps
items.purpose: Runs gap analysis for one compliance framework against the org's active policies.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: analyzeGaps() result (gap analysis object; exact fields not enumerated here)
items.errors: 400 'framework query parameter is required' (+ available list); 404 unknown framework (+ available list); 500 'Internal server error'
items.gotchas: Policies are converted via convertPolicies()/mapPolicies() from getActivePolicies() before analysis — a policy authoring bug shows up here as a gap-analysis discrepancy.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/map
items.purpose: Maps the org's active policies onto one compliance framework's controls, enriched with each control's expected policy_mappings for UI 'create policy from gap' prefill.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: compliance map object with a controls[] array; each control augmented with policy_mappings from the framework definition
items.errors: 400 'framework query parameter is required'; 404 unknown framework; 500 'Internal server error'
items.gotchas: none beyond the gaps route's policy-conversion caveat

items.name: GET /api/compliance/report
items.purpose: Generates a full compliance report (markdown or JSON) for one framework and persists a compliance_snapshots row.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 400 'framework query parameter is required'; 404 unknown framework; 500 'Internal server error'
items.gotchas: Side effect: every GET call writes a new compliance_snapshots row (id cs_<uuid>) even though it's a read endpoint.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/schedules
items.purpose: Lists recurring compliance export schedules for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 'Failed to fetch schedules'
items.gotchas: none

items.name: POST /api/compliance/schedules
items.purpose: Creates a recurring compliance export schedule.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.response: 201 with { id } of the created schedule
items.errors: 400 'frameworks array is required' or 'cron_expression is required'; 500 'Failed to create schedule'
items.gotchas: Route only validates presence of frameworks/cron_expression — no cron syntax validation seen here.

items.name: PATCH /api/compliance/schedules/{scheduleId}
items.purpose: Updates a compliance schedule's enabled flag and/or name.
