items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 404 'Schedule not found'; 500 'Failed to update schedule'
items.gotchas: Only enabled and name are settable via this route — frameworks/cron_expression/format/window_days are not updatable here.

items.name: DELETE /api/compliance/schedules/{scheduleId}
items.purpose: Deletes a compliance schedule.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 'Failed to delete schedule'
items.gotchas: No existence check — DELETE on a non-existent id still returns { deleted: true }.

items.name: GET /api/compliance/trends
items.purpose: Returns historical compliance_snapshots trend data, optionally filtered to one framework.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 'Failed to fetch trends'
items.gotchas: none

items.name: GET /api/coverage
items.purpose: Returns the per-agent coverage summary (expected-vs-recorded actions) that the /agents surface reads.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse (code COVERAGE_GET)
items.gotchas: include_synthetic is an ephemeral diagnostic view — nothing is persisted, and real dashboards/posture never consume it.

items.name: POST /api/coverage
items.purpose: Ingests one per-turn expected-vs-recorded coverage report from the Stop hook (v4.2 coverage truth).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny via authenticateProtectedApi)

inputs.body.recorded: required non-negative integer, capped at 1,000,000 (may legitimately exceed expected — not clamped below it)

items.errors: 400 'Invalid JSON body' or 'Validation failed' (missing/invalid agent_id, expected, or recorded); 500 via apiErrorResponse (code COVERAGE_POST)
items.gotchas: Designed to be fail-silent from the hook's perspective — it's a per-turn evidence report, not a governance decision.

items.name: GET /api/cron/code-session-cache-crater
items.purpose: Scans every project with code sessions for a week-over-week prompt-cache hit-rate collapse ("cache crater") and inserts alerts for projects that regressed.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare on the Authorization header; 503 if CRON_SECRET unset, 401 on mismatch. Public route (/api/cron prefix bypasses middleware auth).
items.response: { ok: true, projects_scanned: number, alerts_inserted: number }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Cache-crater sweep failed' } on unexpected exception
items.gotchas: No GitHub Actions workflow found under .github/workflows/ for this route (unlike jti-sweep/outcome-sweep/integration-health/reset-meters/code-session-weekly-memo, which all have one) — likely not yet wired to a scheduler and must be triggered manually or via an external cron. Computes ISO week boundaries (Mon-start, UTC) for this-week vs prior-week token totals per project. Verified: vercel.json …

items.name: GET /api/cron/code-session-weekly-memo
items.purpose: Generates and saves a weekly markdown memo summarizing each project's Claude Code sessions (compared against the prior week) for projects with activity in the last 7 days.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { ok: true, projects_scanned: number, memos_saved: number }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'weekly memo run failed' }
items.gotchas: Scheduled by .github/workflows/code-session-weekly-memo.yml, cron '0 4 * * 1' (Mondays 04:00 UTC). Skips projects with zero sessions in the last 7 days (memo not generated/saved for them).

items.name: GET /api/cron/integration-health
items.purpose: Polls all configured third-party integrations for every active org, records health-status transitions, and fires alerts when a provider's status changes.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET checked manually with node:crypto timingSafeEqual (not the shared timingSafeCompare helper) plus an explicit 'Bearer ' prefix check to avoid a token-length bypass; 500 if CRON_SECR…
items.response: { ok: true, orgs: number, checked: number, alerts: number }
items.errors: 500 { error: 'CRON_SECRET not set' } (note: 500 not 503, unlike sibling cron routes); 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Health check failed' }
items.gotchas: Optional scheduler at .github/workflows/integration-health.yml, cron '0 */6 * * *' (every 6 hours) — comment in the workflow says it's opt-in for installs without Vercel Pro cron. 'not_configured' providers are skipped (not counted in totalChecked).

items.name: GET /api/cron/jti-sweep
items.purpose: Scheduled GC belt-and-suspenders for expired JTI replay-protection rows and spent OAuth rows (consumed/expired auth codes, revoked/aged access tokens) that the in-line probabilistic sweep (~1% of writes) can leave behind during low-traffic periods.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { ok: true, deleted: number, oauth_purged: number|null }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Sweep failed' }
items.gotchas: Scheduled by .github/workflows/jti-sweep.yml, cron '*/5 * * * *' (every 5 min). OAuth purge is wrapped separately and is best-effort — its failure is logged but does not fail the whole request (oauth_purged stays null in that case). Phase 2b, issue #120.

items.name: GET /api/cron/learning-episodes-backfill
items.purpose: For every org, finds action records not yet scored into a learning episode (within a lookback window) and scores/stores them via the learning loop service.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { success: true, summary: { orgs_processed, actions_considered, episodes_scored }, options: { lookback_days, per_org_limit }, ran_at: ISO string }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Cron job failed' }; per-org failures are caught and logged individually so one bad org doesn't abort the whole run
items.gotchas: No GitHub Actions workflow found for this route — not yet wired to a scheduler. Iterates listOrganizations({includeDefault:true}) so org_default is included, unlike some other cron loops that query organizations directly and exclude it. Verified: vercel.json has no crons block either — this route has no in-repo scheduler and must be invoked by an external scheduler carrying CRON_SECRET.

items.name: GET /api/cron/learning-recommendations
items.purpose: Rebuilds per-org learning recommendations from scored episodes for every organization.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { success: true, summary: { orgs_processed, episodes_scanned, recommendations_generated }, options: {...}, ran_at: ISO string }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Cron job failed' }; per-org errors caught and logged, loop continues
items.gotchas: No GitHub Actions workflow found for this route — not yet wired to a scheduler. Verified: vercel.json has no crons block either — this route has no in-repo scheduler and must be invoked by an external scheduler carrying CRON_SECRET.

items.name: GET /api/cron/memory-maintenance
items.purpose: Runs agent-memory maintenance per org (excluding org_default), notifying agents/sending messages as needed, and logs an audit activity entry for orgs where maintenance actually processed something.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { success: true, summary: { orgs_processed, agents_notified, messages_sent } }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Maintenance job failed' }; per-org errors caught, orgs_processed still incremented
items.gotchas: No GitHub Actions workflow found for this route. Explicitly excludes org_default (`WHERE id != 'org_default'`) unlike learning-episodes-backfill/learning-recommendations which include it via includeDefault:true. Only orgs whose runMemoryMaintenance result.status === 'processed' contribute to agents_notified/messages_sent and get an activity log row. Verified: vercel.json has no crons block either…

items.name: GET /api/cron/outcome-sweep
items.purpose: Sweeps action_records whose outcome timeout has elapsed without an agent-reported outcome ('lost_confirmation'), marks them, publishes an SSE signal event, and fires org webhooks for the resulting signals.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { ok: true, orgs_scanned: number, rows_swept: number, webhooks_fired: number }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Sweep failed' }; webhook delivery failures per-org are caught and logged as warnings without aborting
items.gotchas: Scheduled by .github/workflows/outcome-sweep.yml, cron '*/15 * * * *' (every 15 min — matches the default timeout window). Timeout minutes is per-org, read from settings key DASHCLAW_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (default 15, clamped 1 to 1440); falls back to default on any read error. Only orgs returned by listOrgsWithStaleOutcomes(sql, FLOOR_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=1) are scanned.

items.name: GET /api/cron/policy-suggestions
items.purpose: Generates policy-tightening/loosening suggestions per org from recent action/episode history.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { success: true, results: [{ org_id, suggestion_count, error? }], ran_at: ISO string }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Cron job failed' }; per-org failure is captured inline in the results array (suggestion_count: 0, error: message) rather than aborting the loop
items.gotchas: No GitHub Actions workflow found for this route — not yet wired to a scheduler. Uses listOrganizations({includeDefault:true}). Verified: vercel.json has no crons block either — this route has no in-repo scheduler and must be invoked by an external scheduler carrying CRON_SECRET.

items.name: GET /api/cron/reset-meters
items.purpose: Monthly usage-meter reset: purges usage_meters rows from prior billing periods for per-period resources (governed_actions, capability_invocations, workflow_executions, actions_per_month), leaving the current period and non-period-based ('current') resources intact.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { success: true, period: string, meters_reset: number }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Meter reset failed' }
items.gotchas: Scheduled by .github/workflows/reset-meters.yml, cron '0 0 1 * *' (1st of month, midnight UTC). period comes from getCurrentPeriod() in lib/usage — the DELETE filters period <> current AND period <> 'current' (the synthetic non-period-based marker for resources like members/api_keys), so those are never purged.

items.name: GET /api/cron/signals
items.purpose: Computes risk/health signals for every active org, dedupes against previously-seen signal hashes, upserts snapshots, then fans new signals out to webhooks, native notification integrations, SSE events, and opted-in email subscribers.
items.auth: Bearer CRON_SECRET via timingSafeCompare; 503 if unset, 401 on mismatch.
items.response: { success: true, summary: { orgs_processed, new_signals, emails_sent, webhooks_fired, native_notifications } }
items.errors: 503 CRON_SECRET not configured; 401 Unauthorized; 500 { error: 'Cron job failed' }; per-org processing errors are caught and logged, orgs_processed still increments
items.gotchas: No GitHub Actions workflow found for this route — not yet wired to a scheduler (unusual given this is one of the more consequential signal/notification routes). Dedup fingerprint = sha256(type + agent_id + action_id + loop_id + assumption_id + session_id + provider + policy_id) truncated to 32 hex chars, so a new signal type must add its own id field to hashSignal or it will collide/dedupe incorr…

items.name: POST /api/discord/interactions
items.purpose: Discord interaction webhook for approve/deny buttons on pending-approval messages; resolves the action asynchronously and edits the original Discord message.
items.auth: public route (in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES) — self-authenticates via Ed25519 signature verification (x-signature-ed25519 + x-signature-timestamp headers against DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY, 5-minute anti-re…

inputs.body: raw Discord interaction payload: { type, data:{custom_id: 'ap:<action_id>'|'dn:<action_id>'}, user.id | member.user.id, application_id, token }

items.response: { type: 1 } (PONG) for the handshake/unknown-type/unmatched-button cases; { type: 6 } (DEFERRED_UPDATE_MESSAGE) ack for a recognized approve/deny button click
items.errors: 401 invalid signature or disallowed user (both collapse to the same 401 to avoid an oracle); 400 invalid JSON
items.gotchas: Signature must be verified over the raw body text before JSON.parse (re-serialized JSON breaks it); approval resolution runs asynchronously via next/server after() so the 3-second Discord ack deadline is met; on resolve it edits the original Discord message AND clears any pending Telegram approval notification for the same action (cross-channel resolution); requires DISCORD_APPROVER_ORG_ID env or…

items.name: GET /api/docs/raw
items.purpose: Serves the raw SDK README.md as plain markdown text (used by agents/tools that want to fetch DashClaw SDK docs directly), optionally appending the deprecated legacy v1 SDK's full source.
items.auth: Public — explicitly listed in PUBLIC_ROUTES; no auth check in the handler at all (intentional public read-only content endpoint per middleware.js comment).

inputs.query.legacy: 'true' to append the full deprecated sdk/legacy/dashclaw-v1.js source under a '## Legacy SDK (v1) Full Source' section

items.response: Raw text/markdown body (Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8), not JSON
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Documentation not found' } (JSON, inconsistent content-type with the success path) if sdk/README.md (or the legacy file when legacy=true) can't be read from disk
items.gotchas: Reads directly from the filesystem at request time (readFileSync against process.cwd()) rather than a generated/bundled asset — depends on the sdk/ directory being present in the deployed bundle. Cache-Control: no-cache on success.

items.name: GET /api/doctor
items.purpose: Runs the instance/tenant health-check engine (runDoctor) across categories and returns pass/warn/fail checks with optional remediation hints.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no additional role check in-route

inputs.query.category: comma-separated category list, optional (defaults to all)
inputs.query.include_fixes: string 'false' to omit fix hints, default true

items.response: { status: 'healthy'|'needs_attention'|'unhealthy', summary: { pass, warn, fail }, checks: [...], timestamp }
items.errors: 500 on unexpected engine error ({error: message}); response status is 503 when status === 'unhealthy'
items.gotchas: host is read from the Host header only (never a query param) to avoid SSRF/spoofing in deployment checks; orgId scopes tenant data probes and comes from server-set x-org-id header.

items.name: POST /api/doctor/fix
items.purpose: Applies a named remote fix action from the doctor fix registry, then re-runs doctor and returns the recheck result.
items.auth: admin (x-org-role: admin AND x-org-id header, both server-set by middleware)

inputs.body....params: any extra fields passed through to the fix handler

items.response: { ...fixResult (applied, action, description, ...), recheck: <doctor GET result shape> }
items.errors: 403 if role isn't admin or orgId missing; 400 if action missing; 500 on unexpected error
items.gotchas: Always runs with allowLocal:false (no filesystem/env-file fixes over the API); orgId is always the verified header value, overriding any client-supplied orgId so tenant-scoped fixes (e.g. normalize_timestamps) can't cross orgs; unknown action returns applied:false rather than an error status.

items.name: GET /api/drift/alerts
items.purpose: Lists drift alerts for the org with optional filters.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no additional role check
items.response: { alerts: [...drift_alerts rows], total: number (alerts.length, not a true count) }
items.errors: 500 on query failure
items.gotchas: total is just the returned page length, not a full count.

items.name: POST /api/drift/alerts
items.purpose: Runs a drift operation: detect drift (default), compute baselines, or record snapshots, depending on body.action.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole(request) === 'admin')
items.response: 201 with the result of the chosen operation (detectDrift returns alerts array; computeBaselines/recordSnapshots return per-agent/metric results arrays)
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 500 on operation failure
items.gotchas: action defaults silently to 'detect' if omitted or unrecognized.

items.name: PATCH /api/drift/alerts/{alertId}
items.purpose: Acknowledges a drift alert, stamping acknowledged_by/acknowledged_at.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 404 if alert not found; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: acknowledged_by uses the real session user id when available (getUserId), falling back to the label 'admin (api key)' for API-key principals.

items.name: DELETE /api/drift/alerts/{alertId}
items.purpose: Deletes a drift alert by id.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Delete is unconditional — returns {deleted:true} even if no row matched (no existence check before delete).

items.name: GET /api/drift/metrics
items.purpose: Returns the static list of supported drift metrics (id + label) for populating filter UIs.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 on unexpected error
items.gotchas: Purely static/in-memory (DRIFT_METRICS constant); no DB access.

items.name: GET /api/drift/snapshots
items.purpose: Lists drift_snapshots rows for the org, optionally filtered by agent and/or metric.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: { snapshots: [...drift_snapshots rows ordered by period_start DESC] }
items.errors: 500 on query failure
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: GET /api/drift/stats
items.purpose: Returns aggregate drift alert stats (overall counts by severity/ack) and opportunistically triggers a debounced drift detection tick.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check (tick runs regardless of caller role)
items.response: { ...driftStats (total_alerts, critical_count, warning_count, info_count, unacknowledged, today_count, ...), auto_tick: <tick result or null> }
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: maybeRunDriftTick is debounced to once per 24h per org with a bounded time budget; tick failures are swallowed (logged, never break the stats response) since this route is the natural non-hot-path host for detection (never the guard path).

items.name: GET /api/echo
items.purpose: Returns a static hint describing the echo endpoint's behavior.
items.auth: public (listed in middleware PUBLIC_ROUTES)
items.errors: none
items.gotchas: Public but still rate-limited by middleware; intended as a generic webhook/demo test destination.

items.name: POST /api/echo
items.purpose: Constant-response echo target for webhook test-fires and registry demo seeds.
items.auth: public (listed in middleware PUBLIC_ROUTES)
items.response: { received: true, event: string|null (from x-dashclaw-event header, truncated to 64 chars), at: ISO timestamp }
items.errors: none
items.gotchas: Request body is NEVER read or reflected (deliberately, to avoid storage/abuse); only works as a target against a publicly reachable deployment since outbound SSRF guards block private/loopback hosts.

items.name: GET /api/enforcement-liveness
items.purpose: Latest enforcement-liveness probe runs for the caller's org plus the derived surface state. The probe (hooks/enforcement_liveness_probe.py, auto-spawned by the SessionStart digest at most every 12h) drives a synthetic held action through the real PreToolUse hook seam and verdicts by whether the action executed — never by reading the decision ledger (the v4.72.1 lesson). Human surfaces: /setup#enforcement-liveness card and the Mission Control posture tile.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { runs:[{id, org_id, source, verdict:'held'|'executed'|'unprovable', detail, hook:{installed, settings_path?, timeout_seconds?, effective_timer_ms?, overflowed?, mode?, exit_code?, cancelled?}, witness:{path, executed}, decision, checks:[{id,title,status:'pass'|'fail'|'info',detail?,durationMs?}], started_at, finished_at, created_at}], stale_after_ms: 86400000, state:'holding'|'stale'|'broken' }
items.errors: 400 invalid limit; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: state derives from the latest run and the 24h staleness window: no run within 24h renders 'stale' (a probe that silently stopped running is itself the v4.72.1 failure shape and must not render green); verdict 'executed' or 'unprovable' renders 'broken'. Probe runs land in enforcement_liveness_runs only — never action_records/guard_decisions (live-canary precedent).

items.name: POST /api/enforcement-liveness
items.purpose: Files an enforcement-liveness probe verdict. Called by hooks/enforcement_liveness_probe.py after it runs the installed pretool hook under harness-faithful timeout semantics (timeout is SECONDS; seconds*1000 past int32 overflows the harness timer and cancels the hook fail-open) and observes the witness.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.hook: object, required — installed (boolean, required) + whitelisted diagnostics (settings_path, timeout_seconds, effective_timer_ms, overflowed, mode, exit_code, cancelled)
inputs.body.checks: array 1-50 of {id, title, status pass|fail|info, detail?, durationMs?}, required
inputs.body.decision: string ≤200, optional — recorded guard decision, diagnosis only

items.errors: 400 per-field validation errors naming the field; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: Inserting prunes the org's runs older than 30 days in the same call (retention rides along, no cron). Unknown hook fields are dropped, wrong-typed known fields are rejected. Runs are structurally excluded from posture scoring, calibration mining, and funnel truth by never touching the action/guard ledgers.

items.name: GET /api/evaluations
items.purpose: Lists eval scores (eval_scores rows) with filters.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: result of listEvalScores (rows + pagination info per repository)
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: none notable beyond standard org scoping.

items.name: POST /api/evaluations
items.purpose: Creates a single evaluation score row directly (not via a scorer run).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 400 missing required fields or score out of [0,1] range; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: id is generated as `ev_<24 hex chars>`; score is strictly validated as a number between 0.0 and 1.0.

items.name: GET /api/evaluations/runs
items.purpose: Lists eval_runs for the org, optionally filtered by status.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: POST /api/evaluations/runs
items.purpose: Creates an eval run (status 'pending') and executes it asynchronously after the response is sent via Next's after().
items.auth: admin/owner (getOrgRole in ['admin','owner'])

inputs.body.name: required
inputs.body.scorer_id: required, must reference an existing eval_scorers row

items.errors: 403 if not admin/owner; 400 if name/scorer_id missing or scorer_type is llm_judge with no AI provider configured (checks isLLMAvailable); 404 if scorer not found; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Execution is fire-and-after (Vercel-safe via after()) — the response returns 'pending' immediately; the run's actual scoring happens post-response and failures are only logged server-side, not surfaced to the caller. created_by uses the real session user id, falling back to the role string.

items.name: GET /api/evaluations/runs/{runId}
items.purpose: Fetches a single eval run's details plus score distribution.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: { run: {...eval_runs joined with scorer name/type}, distribution: [...score distribution rows] } (from getEvalRun)
items.errors: 404 if run not found; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: distribution is scoped to exactly this run via run_id (previously it aggregated across all runs sharing the scorer).

items.name: PATCH /api/evaluations/runs/{runId}
items.purpose: Updates an eval run's status.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: No-op (still returns {updated:true}) if body.status is falsy — nothing is actually updated in that case; no existence check on runId.

items.name: GET /api/evaluations/scorers
items.purpose: Lists eval scorers for the org along with total_scores/avg_score aggregates per scorer and whether an LLM provider is configured.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: { scorers: [...eval_scorers rows with total_scores, avg_score], llm_available: boolean }
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: POST /api/evaluations/scorers
items.purpose: Creates an evaluation scorer definition.
items.auth: admin/owner (getOrgRole in ['admin','owner'])

inputs.body.name: required, must be unique per org

items.response: 201 { id: 'es_<hex>', name, scorer_type, config, description, created_at, warning? }
items.errors: 403 if not admin/owner; 400 missing fields or invalid scorer_type; 409 duplicate name (unique/duplicate constraint violation); 500 on failure
items.gotchas: If scorer_type is llm_judge and no AI provider key is configured, response includes a non-fatal `warning` field rather than blocking creation.

items.name: POST /api/evaluations/scorers/preview
items.purpose: Dry-runs a scorer config against a sample action record without persisting any eval_scores row — for validating a scorer before creating it.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check

inputs.body.sample: optional plain object — a partial action_records row (outcome, action_type, risk_score, declared_goal, status, plus any numeric field a numeric_range scorer references)

items.response: { preview: true, scorer_type, result: { score, label, reasoning, error } }
items.errors: 400 if scorer_type missing/invalid or sample is not a plain object; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Side-effect-free — uses the same executeScorer() engine as real runs but never writes eval_scores; llm_judge degrades to a structured error result (not an HTTP error) when no AI provider is configured.

items.name: PATCH /api/evaluations/scorers/{scorerId}
items.purpose: Updates a scorer's name/description/config.
items.auth: admin/owner (getOrgRole in ['admin','owner'])
items.errors: 403 if not admin/owner; 400 if no recognized fields supplied; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Only name/description/config are accepted; scorer_type cannot be changed via PATCH.

items.name: DELETE /api/evaluations/scorers/{scorerId}
items.purpose: Deletes a scorer.
items.auth: admin/owner (getOrgRole in ['admin','owner'])
items.errors: 403 if not admin/owner; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: No existence check — returns deleted:true regardless of whether a row matched.

items.name: GET /api/evaluations/stats
items.purpose: Returns aggregate evaluation statistics (overall, by-scorer, trends, distribution) over a lookback window.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: cutoff is computed as now - days*24h and compared against eval_scores.created_at::timestamptz (created_at is TEXT under the hood).

items.name: GET /api/finops/spend
items.purpose: Returns a spend rollup for the org, either the fleet lens (agent LLM cost + x402 spend) or the claude-code lens (operator Claude Code session token cost).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check

inputs.query.agent_id: optional, fleet lens only — ignored for claude-code lens

items.response: fleet: { lens:'fleet', period, agent, x402, fleet_total_usd, unpriced }; claude-code: { lens:'claude_code', period, code_sessions, code_total_usd }
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: fleet_total_usd = agent LLM cost + x402 spend by design invariant; claude-code lens ignores agent_id since code_sessions have no agent dimension; code cost is advisory (governed:false), already billed at ingest time.

items.name: GET /api/guard
items.purpose: List recent guard decisions for the org, with optional filters by agent, decision outcome, and time window.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.query.decision: optional filter (e.g. block, allow, warn, require_approval)
inputs.query.days: optional, clamped 1-90; when set, windows both the returned rows AND the `total` count

items.response: 200: { decisions/results per listGuardDecisions, total, limit, offset } (fields spread from listGuardDecisions result plus limit/offset).
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse for unexpected errors.
items.gotchas: An unconfigured self-host org ('org_default') simply returns empty results rather than erroring — no special-case bypass needed. Passing both `decision` and `days` gives the true windowed denied-count via `total`.

items.name: POST /api/guard
items.purpose: The core policy-decision endpoint. Evaluates a proposed agent action against org guard policies and returns allow/warn/block/require_approval, optionally also creating the running action record in the same call.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate. Optionally also accepts an `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` for Phase 2 cryptographic agent-identity verification…

inputs.body.declared_goal: string, max 2000 (alias: intent), scanned for prompt-injection patterns (blocks with 400 on 'block' recommendation)
inputs.body.target: string, max 1024, optional — act-binding resource target
inputs.body.content: string, max 50000, optional — outbound content; auto-scanned for secrets (warn by default, or hard-block if org setting DASHCLAW_AUTOSCAN_BLOCK=true)
inputs.body.idempotency_key: string, max 256, optional — enables end-to-end replay dedupe (10 min window)
inputs.body.act: object, optional evidence payload — { kind: 'shell'|'http'|'sql'|'file', ...kind-specific fields }, max 16KB serialized
inputs.body.harness_session_id: string, sanitized to <=200 chars else null (fleet attribution, not validated by schema)
inputs.body.subagent_uuid: string, sanitized to <=200 chars else null (fleet attribution, not validated by schema)
inputs.query.include_signals: 'true' to add live signal warnings via computeSignals
inputs.query.record: 'true' to additionally create the running action_records row in this same call (same insert as POST /api/actions) and return action_id

items.response: 200: { decision: allow|warn|block|require_approval, decision_id, action_id (deprecated alias of decision_id), reason, signals, matched_policies, non_fabrication? , risk_score, agent_risk_score, risk_breakdown, intent_source, derived_action_type?, evidence_mismatch?, verification_status, agent_id, agent_name, evaluated_at, learning?, recovery?, predictive_risk?, degraded?, reasons (legacy), warnin…
items.errors: 400 Invalid JSON body; 400 Validation failed (details: field errors); 400 prompt-injection detected (risk_level, categories); 200 (not 4xx) hard secret-block returns decision: 'block' when DASHCLAW_AUTOSCAN_BLOCK is on; 500 via apiErrorResponse for …
items.gotchas: Org halt (POST /api/halt) forces an immediate block and bypasses the idempotency replay cache so a halted org can't be masked by a retried pre-halt decision. ?record=true never records when decision is 'block', when agent_id/declared_goal are missing, or when the org's actions_per_month quota is exceeded (recorded:false with a reason). Guard has an internal evaluation deadline; on timeout or inte…

items.name: GET /api/guard/decisions
items.purpose: List guardrail (guard) decisions for a dashboard-style view, parsing stored JSON columns and joining aggregate stats in one call.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { decisions: [{ ...row, matched_policies (parsed array), context: undefined, declared_goal (from parsed context), agent_name (from parsed context) }], total, stats: {blocks, approvals, warns} (7-day counts of block / require_approval / warn decisions) }.
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse for unexpected errors.
items.gotchas: Malformed stored JSON in matched_policies or context is tolerated best-effort (falls back to [] / {}) rather than erroring the whole list. This is a distinct route/table path from GET /api/guard (guardrails.repository vs guard.repository) — used by a different UI surface.

items.name: GET /api/halt
items.purpose: Returns the org's kill-switch (org halt) state.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { halt: { halted: boolean, actor: string|null, reason: string|null, at: string|null } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: State is stored as a JSON-encoded settings row under key DASHCLAW_ORG_HALT, category 'general'.

items.name: POST /api/halt
items.purpose: Sets or clears the org-wide kill switch; while halted, every guard evaluation for the org immediately blocks (still recorded/audited).
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { ok: true, halt: { halted, actor, reason, at } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if halted is not a boolean; standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: Invalidates the guard settings cache eagerly (invalidateGuardSettingsCache) so the switch takes effect immediately rather than after the ~30s guard cache TTL; writes an activity_logs audit row (org.halted / org.resumed); actor uses real user id, falling back to 'admin'.

items.name: GET /api/handoffs
items.purpose: List code-session handoff bundles for an agent/project (most-recent first), or with ?latest=true return only the single most recent unconsumed handoff.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie).

inputs.query.agent_id: optional filter; required (400 if missing) when latest=true

items.response: Default: 200 { handoffs: [{ id, agent_id, project_id, bundle, created_at, consumed_at }], total }. With ?latest=true: 200 { id, agent_id, project_id, bundle, created_at } (no consumed_at/total).
items.errors: 400 agent_id required (only in latest=true mode); 404 { error: 'no_handoff' } when latest=true finds nothing; 500 via apiErrorResponse.
items.gotchas: Same GET handler serves two distinct response shapes depending on ?latest=true — used by both Node/Python SDKs (getLatestHandoff/get_handoffs) and the dashboard Handoffs tab, which previously 405'd because only POST existed.

items.name: POST /api/handoffs
items.purpose: Create a new code-session handoff bundle for an agent, to be picked up by a later session (context continuity across sessions).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie).
items.errors: 400 agent_id required; 400 bundle (object) required; 500 via apiErrorResponse.
items.gotchas: Body is JSON-parsed with a catch-to-{} fallback, so a malformed body surfaces as the field-required 400s rather than a raw parse error.

items.name: GET /api/handoffs/{id}
items.purpose: Fetch a single handoff bundle by its id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie).
items.response: 200: { id, agent_id, project_id, bundle, created_at, consumed_at }.
items.errors: 404 { error: 'not_found' } if the handoff doesn't exist (or belongs to a different org); 500 via apiErrorResponse.
items.gotchas: Lookup is org-scoped (getHandoffById(sql, orgId, id)) — a handoff id from another org returns 404, not 403.

items.name: POST /api/handoffs/{id}/consume
items.purpose: Mark a handoff as consumed by the session that picked it up, recording which session consumed it.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie).

inputs.body.session_id: string, optional — the consuming session's id

items.errors: 404 { error: 'not_found' } if the handoff doesn't exist for this org; 500 via apiErrorResponse.
items.gotchas: Body is JSON-parsed with a catch-to-{} fallback, so session_id is fully optional and a malformed body doesn't error the call.

items.name: GET /api/handoffs/latest
items.purpose: Standalone endpoint returning the single most recent unconsumed handoff for an agent (functionally identical to GET /api/handoffs?latest=true).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie).
items.errors: 400 agent_id required; 404 { error: 'no_handoff' }; 500 via apiErrorResponse.
items.gotchas: Duplicates the ?latest=true branch of GET /api/handoffs as a dedicated path — kept for callers that prefer an explicit URL over a query flag.

items.name: GET /api/health
items.purpose: System health check for monitoring — reports DB connectivity, realtime backend health, embeddings status, and required env vars.
items.auth: None. /api/health is listed in middleware.js's PUBLIC_ROUTES array (line 37) — fully public, no x-api-key or session required. Confirmed by reading middleware.js.
items.response: 200 or 503: { status: 'healthy'|'degraded', timestamp, version, mode: 'demo'|'live', checks: { behavioral_ai: { active, engine }, database: { status }, runtime: { edge_compatible, node_env }, realtime: {...}, environment: { status, missing? } } }.
items.errors: Returns 503 (not a thrown error) whenever any check reports degraded/unhealthy — e.g. missing core DB tables, missing DATABASE_URL/NEXTAUTH_SECRET, or realtime backend unhealthy.
items.gotchas: Deliberately never leaks backend error details or auth-config status on this public endpoint (comments explicitly call this out as a security measure). `mode` reflects DASHCLAW_MODE or NEXT_PUBLIC_DASHCLAW_MODE env var, used by the Python hook to warn if pointed at a demo instance.

items.name: GET /api/hosted/capacity
items.purpose: Reports whether the hosted trial pool is full (active trial count vs configured max).
items.auth: public (middleware isHostedPublicRequest allows GET on this exact path; route also self-guards with isHostedMode)
items.response: { full: boolean, active: number, max: number }
items.errors: 404 if not in hosted mode
items.gotchas: Aggregate-only (no org identifiers).

items.name: POST /api/hosted/cleanup
items.purpose: Deletes expired hosted trial workspaces (cross-tenant sweep), up to 100 per call.
items.auth: cron/operator secret (x-cleanup-secret header matching HOSTED_CLEANUP_SECRET, OR Authorization: Bearer matching CRON_SECRET, both via timing-safe compare) OR operator-admin fallback (x-org-role owner…
items.response: { found: number, deleted: number, errors: [{ orgId, error }] }
items.errors: 404 if not hosted mode; 403 if neither the cleanup secret nor a valid non-trial admin/owner principal is presented
items.gotchas: A trial-org's own admin role is explicitly denied (cross-tenant destructive risk) — only the secret path or a genuine operator/non-trial org can trigger cleanup.

items.name: GET /api/hosted/funnel
items.purpose: Returns the aggregate trial activation funnel (conversion rates, cohort trends) with a 60s in-memory cache.
items.auth: public (middleware isHostedPublicRequest allows GET on this exact path; route also self-guards with isHostedMode)
items.errors: 404 if not hosted mode
items.gotchas: 60-second per-instance in-memory cache (module-level variable, not per-request) so an unauthenticated hot loop hits memory, not the DB; discloses more than /api/hosted/capacity (conversion rates/trends) but no org ids, slugs, or key prefixes.

items.name: GET /api/hosted/workspaces
items.purpose: Not implemented — explicitly rejects GET on the collection route.
items.auth: n/a
items.errors: 405 Method Not Allowed with Allow: POST header
items.gotchas: Only POST is implemented on this path despite the inventory listing GET,POST.

items.name: POST /api/hosted/workspaces
items.purpose: Provisions a new hosted trial workspace (org + API key) after Cloudflare Turnstile verification and per-IP daily rate limiting; optionally mints a trial session cookie.
items.auth: public (middleware isHostedPublicRequest allows POST on this exact path; route also self-guards with isHostedMode)

inputs.body.turnstile_token: required for Turnstile verification (empty allowed but will fail verification)
inputs.body.source: optional, resolved to a mint-source channel label (spoofable by design, for attribution only)

items.response: { workspace_id, api_key, key_prefix, endpoint, expires_at, trial_action_cap, session: boolean, next_steps_url }
items.errors: 400 turnstile verification failed; 429 rate limit exceeded (retry_after_ms); 503 trials are full; 500 provisioning failed
items.gotchas: Turnstile is verified BEFORE consuming a rate-limit slot so bad-token bot requests don't burn legitimate users' quota; client IP resolution trusts x-forwarded-for/x-real-ip only when TRUST_PROXY or VERCEL env indicates a trusted proxy, else falls back to a shared 'unknown' bucket; session cookie is only minted if NEXTAUTH_SECRET is set (otherwise `session:false` and a console warning, but the key…

items.name: GET /api/hosted/workspaces/{workspaceId}
items.purpose: Instance-operator inspection of a specific hosted workspace's trial state.
items.auth: operator/admin (x-org-role owner/admin AND not a trial principal, via denyTrialPrincipal) — NOT reachable via the hosted-public path
items.errors: 404 if not hosted mode, workspace not found, or not a hosted workspace; 403 if not operator/non-trial admin
items.gotchas: A trial org's own admin role is denied here — role alone would let trial A read trial B (cross-tenant); only a genuine operator (non-trial org) with owner/admin role passes.

items.name: DELETE /api/hosted/workspaces/{workspaceId}
items.purpose: Instance-operator deletion of a specific hosted workspace.
items.auth: operator/admin (x-org-role owner/admin AND not a trial principal, via denyTrialPrincipal)
items.errors: 404 if not hosted mode, workspace not found, or the id is 'not a hosted' workspace; 403 if not operator/non-trial admin; 500 on unexpected failure
items.gotchas: Cross-tenant destructive op — deliberately excluded from the hosted-public route table in middleware; same trial-principal denial as GET.

items.name: GET /api/integrations/health
items.purpose: Returns the last-checked health status for each configured integration provider.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Read-only snapshot of stored rows — does not trigger a fresh check (use the refresh route for that).

items.name: POST /api/integrations/health/refresh
items.purpose: Runs an on-demand health check across all configured integrations, upserts results, fires alerts on status transitions, and returns the refreshed health map. Free-tier alternative to the Bearer-authed cron endpoint.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { checked: number, alerts: number, health: { [provider]: { status, message, checked_at } } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: maxDuration 60s; skips providers with status 'not_configured'; alerts only fire for providers whose status actually changed (fireHealthChangeAlerts); prev_status may be null for a fresh row.

items.name: GET /api/integrity/jwks
items.purpose: Serves the public JWKS used to independently re-verify DashClaw-issued proof receipts and signed compliance bundles.
items.auth: public (listed in middleware PUBLIC_ROUTES; also aliased at /.well-known/jwks.json via next.config rewrite)
items.response: { keys: [...] } (standard JWKS shape, public halves only — never includes the `d` private member)
items.errors: Never returns 500 — on internal failure it falls back to { keys: [] } with status 200
items.gotchas: Cache-Control is 'public, max-age=300' only when keys are non-empty; an empty key set is served with 'no-store' so a pre-key-generation fetch never gets pinned at the edge.

items.name: POST /api/integrity/verify
items.purpose: Independently re-verifies a proof receipt or signed compliance bundle against the instance's published JWKS. Stateless — does not look up the original record.
items.auth: public (listed in middleware PUBLIC_ROUTES)
items.response: receipt: { ok: boolean, kid?, reason? }; bundle: verifyBundle result which also echoes prevBundleHash
items.errors: 400 if neither receipt nor bundle provided; never a true 500 — internal errors return 200 { ok:false, reason:'verification_error' } (fail-closed as a non-verification, not a server error)
items.gotchas: For receipts, tries the key whose kid matches the receipt signature first, then falls back to trying every published key; verifying a full bundle chain requires walking successive prevBundleHash links yourself.

items.name: POST /api/internal/resolve-key
items.purpose: Internal bridge used by edge middleware to resolve an API key hash to org/role on self-host deployments with a non-Neon (TCP-only) Postgres, since the edge Neon HTTP driver can't reach it.
items.auth: internal (x-internal-auth header must timing-safe match DASHCLAW_API_KEY, the instance operator key; middleware attaches this on the internal hop and nothing external can forge it)
items.response: { resolved: { keyId, orgId, role, hostedMode, trialEndsAt, trialActionCap, trialActionsUsed } | null, code? }
items.errors: 404 if not self-host mode or if DATABASE_URL is a Neon URL (route is a no-op everywhere else); 401 if x-internal-auth missing/invalid or DASHCLAW_API_KEY unset; 400 if keyHash missing; 500 on transient DB failure (with Postgres error `code` included…
items.gotchas: Deliberately 404s on Neon/hosted so it can never become a hash->org lookup oracle in those environments, even though the path itself is in middleware's PUBLIC_ROUTES; fires a non-blocking touchKeyLastUsed update on successful resolution.

items.name: GET /api/knowledge/collections
items.purpose: Lists knowledge collections for the org, optionally filtered by source_type.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: POST /api/knowledge/collections
items.purpose: Creates a knowledge collection (a named container for ingested/embedded source documents).
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check

inputs.body.name: required
inputs.body.source_type: optional, defaults to 'files'; must be one of the allowed SOURCE_TYPES set
inputs.body.collection_id: optional, auto-generated as kc_<uuid> if omitted

items.errors: 400 if name missing or source_type invalid; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: collection defaults ingestion_status/doc_count via the insert; source_type validation errors are distinguished from other errors by message prefix ('source_type').

items.name: GET /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}
items.purpose: Fetches a single knowledge collection by id.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 404 if not found; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: PATCH /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}
items.purpose: Updates a knowledge collection's fields.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check

inputs.body....fields: collection fields to update, validated by updateCollection (e.g. source_type must still be valid)

items.errors: 404 if not found; 400 if source_type invalid; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: none notable.

items.name: DELETE /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}
items.purpose: Deletes a knowledge collection.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 404 if not found; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: none notable (does not explicitly document cascade to items/chunks in this file — verify repository for cascade behavior).

items.name: GET /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}/items
items.purpose: Lists items within a knowledge collection.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: Does not 404 if the collection itself doesn't exist — just returns an empty items list (no existence check in this GET, unlike POST).

items.name: POST /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}/items
items.purpose: Adds a source item (by URI) to a knowledge collection for later ingestion.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check

inputs.body.title: optional
inputs.body.item_id: optional, auto-generated as kci_<uuid> if omitted

items.response: 201 { item: <inserted knowledge_collection_items row, status defaults e.g. 'pending'> }
items.errors: 400 if source_uri missing; 404 if collection not found; 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: Item is created with a pending/unprocessed status — actual ingestion/embedding happens via the separate sync route, not on add.

items.name: POST /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}/search
items.purpose: Semantic search over a collection's chunked/embedded content using pgvector cosine distance against a BYOK OpenAI-embedded query.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: { query, collection_id, results: [...chunks with similarity scores + source metadata], count }
items.errors: 404 if collection not found; 400 if query missing/blank, or if a BYOK OpenAI API key error occurs ('API key' in message); 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: Requires a BYOK OpenAI key configured for embeddings; errors mentioning 'API key' are surfaced as 400 rather than 500.

items.name: POST /api/knowledge/collections/{collectionId}/sync
items.purpose: Ingests all pending items in a collection inline: fetches each source_uri, chunks content, generates BYOK OpenAI embeddings, and stores knowledge_chunks; updates item/collection status.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 404 if collection not found; 400 if a BYOK OpenAI API key error occurs ('API key' in message); 500 via apiErrorResponse
items.gotchas: Runs synchronously inline (no background worker) and is bounded to 50 items per call, by design for Vercel free-tier duration limits — larger backlogs need repeated calls.

items.name: GET /api/learning
items.purpose: Returns recent decisions, live-consolidated lessons/drift-warnings, and summary stats (success rate, pattern count) for the learning surface.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: { decisions: [...], lessons: [...], drift_warnings: [...], stats: { totalDecisions, totalLessons, successRate, totalWithOutcome, patterns }, lastUpdated }
items.errors: 500 with { error, decisions:[], lessons:[], stats:{} } fallback shape on failure
items.gotchas: Lessons are NOT read from a persisted 'lessons' table (none exists) — they're live-consolidated from learning_recommendations + open drift alerts via consolidateLessons, degrading to empty on failure without breaking the decisions ledger; successRate excludes 'pending' outcomes from its denominator; tolerates a missing decisions/outcomes table (Postgres 42P01) by returning an empty decisions list…

items.name: POST /api/learning
items.purpose: Records a new decision row directly (decision/context/reasoning/outcome/confidence/agent_id) and publishes a DECISION_CREATED org event.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.errors: 400 if decision missing, field length limits exceeded, or unknown fields present (only decision/context/reasoning/outcome/confidence/agent_id accepted); 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Rejects (400) rather than silently drops unknown body fields like legacy `type`/`category`/`tags` since the decisions table has no such columns; publishes an EVENTS.DECISION_CREATED event fire-and-forget (void, not awaited).

items.name: GET /api/learning/analytics/curves
items.purpose: Fetch stored learning-curve windows (per agent/action_type weekly buckets) from learning_curves.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi; getOrgId(request) scopes to org
items.response: { curves: Array<learning_curves row: id, org_id, agent_id, action_type, window_start, window_end, episode_count, avg_score, success_rate, avg_duration_ms, avg_cost, p25_score, p75_score> }
items.errors: 500 on any DB/unexpected error ('Failed to fetch curve data')
items.gotchas: Read-only view over data written by the POST; requires learning_curves table to exist (no schema_missing fallback here, unlike lessons/recommendations).

items.name: POST /api/learning/analytics/curves
items.purpose: Compute weekly learning curves per agent+action_type from learning_episodes and upsert into learning_curves.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.agent_id: string, optional (default: all agents with episodes, up to 50)

items.response: 201 { curves_computed: number, results: Array<{ agent_id, action_type, window_start, count }> }
items.errors: 500 ('Failed to compute curves')
items.gotchas: Skips agent/action_type combos with <3 episodes; groups by 7-day windows; ON CONFLICT (org_id, agent_id, action_type, window_start) upsert; can scan many agents/action_types serially (no explicit cap beyond 20 action types, 50 agents).

items.name: GET /api/learning/analytics/maturity
items.purpose: Return the static maturity-level rubric (thresholds for novice→master classification).
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: { levels: Array<{ level, min_episodes, min_success_rate, min_avg_score }> } — 6 fixed levels: novice, developing, competent, proficient, expert, master
items.errors: 500 ('Failed to fetch maturity levels') — unlikely since it's a static constant, no DB call
items.gotchas: No DB access at all; purely a static lookup table also used internally by velocity computation to classify agents.

items.name: GET /api/learning/analytics/summary
items.purpose: Aggregate dashboard summary: overall episode stats, per-agent leaderboard, per-action-type breakdown, latest velocity, and recommendation effectiveness.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional — filters/collapses all sections to one agent

items.response: { overall: {total_episodes, avg_score, success_count, failure_count, pending_count, avg_duration_ms, total_cost, success_rate}, by_agent: [...], by_action_type: [...], recommendations: {...}, velocity: [...] }
items.errors: 500 on unexpected DB error (no try/catch in route itself — errors bubble to Next's default handler, effectively 500)
items.gotchas: 5 separate SQL aggregates joined in JS (episode stats, per-agent, per-action-type, latest velocity per agent via DISTINCT ON, recommendation effectiveness); no explicit error handling wrapper unlike sibling routes.

items.name: GET /api/learning/analytics/velocity
items.purpose: Fetch stored per-agent velocity/acceleration/maturity records from learning_velocity.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: { velocity: Array<learning_velocity row: id, org_id, agent_id, period, period_start, period_end, episode_count, avg_score, success_rate, score_delta, velocity, acceleration, maturity_score, maturity_level, created_at> }
items.errors: 500 ('Failed to fetch velocity data')
items.gotchas: Read-only; data populated only by the POST variant.

items.name: POST /api/learning/analytics/velocity
items.purpose: Compute learning velocity (slope of avg score over time windows) and acceleration per agent, upsert into learning_velocity, classify maturity.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: 201 { agents_computed: number, results: Array<{ agent_id, episode_count, avg_score, success_rate, score_delta, velocity, acceleration, maturity: {level, score}, windows }> }
items.errors: 500 ('Failed to compute velocity')
items.gotchas: Skips agents with <3 episodes or <2 non-empty time windows; ON CONFLICT (org_id, agent_id, period) upsert — one row per agent per period type, re-running overwrites prior computation.

items.name: GET /api/learning/code-signals
items.purpose: Aggregate code-session signal findings (by kind) over a rolling window for the Code Sessions learning surface.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.query.period: '7d'|'30d'|'90d', optional, default 30d (invalid values fall back to 30d)

items.response: { period, days, findings: Array<{ kind, occurrence_count, session_count, total_savings_usd }> }
items.errors: no explicit try/catch — unhandled errors from aggregateCodeSignalsByKind bubble as 500
items.gotchas: force-dynamic/no-cache; total_savings_usd coerced via Number() to avoid string-from-Postgres-numeric issue.

items.name: GET /api/learning/export
items.purpose: Render an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md operating-notes markdown file from recorded decisions + learned recommendations, served as a downloadable attachment.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: 200 text/markdown body with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="AGENTS.md" or "CLAUDE.md"
items.errors: 500 JSON ('An error occurred generating the export') on unexpected failure
items.gotchas: Tolerates missing learning_recommendations/decisions tables (42P01 or 'does not exist' → treated as empty, not an error); limits both decisions and recommendations to 200 rows; Cache-Control: no-store.

items.name: GET /api/learning/lessons
items.purpose: Consolidate learned lessons (hints/guidance per action_type) plus drift warnings for an agent.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.query.limit: string int, optional, default 10 (no explicit cap in route)

items.response: { lessons: Array<{ action_type, confidence, success_rate, hints: {risk_cap, prefer_reversible, confidence_floor, expected_duration, expected_cost}, guidance, sample_size }>, drift_warnings: Array<{ metric, severity, z_score, direction }>, agent_id }
items.errors: 500 ('Internal server error')
items.gotchas: consolidateLessons degrades gracefully (empty sections) when learning_recommendations/drift_alerts tables are missing, per code comment in learning-lessons.ts.

items.name: GET /api/learning/recommendations
items.purpose: List active learning recommendations for an org/agent, optionally including effectiveness metrics and firing 'fetched' tracking events.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi; include_inactive requires role admin or service

inputs.query.track_events: 'true'|other, optional — fires fetched events when agent_id given

items.response: { recommendations: [...], metrics: object|undefined, lookback_days, total, lastUpdated } — on missing schema: { recommendations: [], metrics: null, lookback_days: 30, total: 0, schema_missing: true, lastUpdated }
items.errors: 500 with recommendations:[] fallback on unexpected error; graceful degrade (not 500) when learning-loop schema tables (42P01/'does not exist') are absent
items.gotchas: track_events fires a fire-and-forget event-recording call (not awaited, errors only warn-logged); include_inactive silently ignored (forced false) for non-admin/service roles rather than 403ing.

items.name: POST /api/learning/recommendations
items.purpose: Rebuild learning recommendations from scored episodes; optionally scores a single action episode first.
items.auth: operator/admin or service role required (getOrgRole(request) must be 'admin' or 'service'), plus base x-api-key/session/OAuth bearer auth

inputs.body.action_id: string, optional, up to 128 chars — if set, scores that episode before rebuilding

items.response: { scored_episode: object|null, episodes_scanned: number, recommendations: [...], total: number, rebuilt_at: ISO timestamp }
items.errors: 403 'Admin or service role required' if role check fails; 400 'Validation failed' with details array on bad body fields; 500 on unexpected error
items.gotchas: Body validation is manual (validatePostBody helper) with bounded-int parsing; if action_id provided, scoreAndStoreActionEpisode runs before the rebuild (extra write side effect).

items.name: POST /api/learning/recommendations/events
items.purpose: Record one or a batch of learning-recommendation lifecycle events (fetched/applied/overridden/outcome).
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.events: array of event objects, optional (single event may be passed as top-level body instead); max 100 per batch
inputs.body.event_type: required per event: one of fetched|applied|overridden|outcome

items.errors: 400 'At least one event is required' (empty array); 400 'events exceeds maximum batch size of 100'; 400 'Validation failed' with per-index details array; 500 on unexpected error
items.gotchas: Accepts either { events: [...] } or a bare single event object as the whole body.

items.name: GET /api/learning/recommendations/metrics
items.purpose: Compute effectiveness metrics for learning recommendations against recent episodes.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi; include_inactive requires admin/service role
items.response: { ...metrics fields from getLearningRecommendationMetrics, lookback_days, lastUpdated } — on missing schema: { metrics: [], summary: {}, lookback_days: 30, schema_missing: true, lastUpdated }
items.errors: 500 ('An error occurred while fetching learning recommendation metrics'); graceful degrade on 42P01/missing-table errors
items.gotchas: Always fetches up to 10000 episodes to compute metrics — potentially heavy query on large orgs.

items.name: PATCH /api/learning/recommendations/{recommendationId}
items.purpose: Toggle a learning recommendation's active flag.
items.auth: operator/admin or service role required (getOrgRole must be 'admin' or 'service')
items.errors: 403 'Admin or service role required'; 400 'active must be a boolean'; 404 'Recommendation not found'; 500 on unexpected error
items.gotchas: Scoped to org via orgId + recommendationId — cross-org IDs return 404, not leaked.

items.name: GET /api/learning/suggestions
items.purpose: Generate candidate guard policy suggestions derived from negative feedback trends.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: { suggestions: Array<{ type, trigger, agent_id, action_type, evidence, suggested_policy: {name, policy_type, rules, agent_ids} }> }
items.errors: 500 ('Internal server error')
items.gotchas: Suggestions are computed on-demand each call (not persisted) — index into the array via suggestion_index is only stable within one GET/POST pair, not across calls.

items.name: POST /api/learning/suggestions
items.purpose: Accept a generated policy suggestion by index, creating a real guard_policies row from it.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.suggestion_index: number — index into a freshly regenerated suggestions list

items.response: { accepted: true, policy: inserted guard_policies row }
items.errors: 400 'Invalid action. Use "accept".' for non-accept actions; 404 'Suggestion not found' if index out of range; 500 ('Internal server error')
items.gotchas: Regenerates suggestions fresh on POST (does not reuse the list from a prior GET) — suggestion_index race: if underlying feedback data changed between GET and POST, the index may point to a different suggestion.

items.name: GET /api/live-canary
items.purpose: Return the org's most recent live-host canary run(s) — production probe results from the hourly GitHub Actions cron.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.errors: 400 'invalid limit: expected an integer between 1 and 20'; apiErrorResponse-shaped error on DB failure
items.gotchas: Read side of a write-only-by-cron feature; runs never touch action/guard ledgers so they're invisible to posture scoring/calibration.

items.name: POST /api/live-canary
items.purpose: Record a live-host canary run verdict (production probe results) filed by the hourly GitHub Actions cron script.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.checks: array of 1-50 {id, title, status:'pass'|'fail', detail?, target?, durationMs?}, required

items.errors: 400 'invalid <field>: <reason>' for any malformed body/check field; apiErrorResponse on DB failure
items.gotchas: Deliberately never writes to action_records or guard_decisions — keeps canary traffic invisible to posture/calibration by design.

items.name: GET /api/secrets
items.purpose: Lists managed secrets metadata for the org (optionally filtered by agent_id) — never the plaintext value.
items.auth: x-api-key
items.response: { secrets: [{ id, org_id, agent_id, name, last_rotated_at, rotation_interval_days, notes, created_at, updated_at, has_value: boolean, value_set_at, delivery_enabled, next_rotation_due }] }
items.errors: structured via apiErrorResponse(err, 'SECRETS_GET') — DB/connection errors surface with the project's standard shape
items.gotchas: has_value is a derived boolean (value_encrypted IS NOT NULL); value_encrypted/plaintext is never selected here (write-only secret values, per project convention).

items.name: POST /api/secrets
items.purpose: Creates a new managed secret record (metadata only — no value set here).
items.auth: x-api-key + operator/admin (getOrgRole(req) !== 'admin' -> 403; server-side gate, headers are middleware-verified so spoofing is not possible)
items.errors: 403 { error: 'Admin access required to create secrets' }; 400 { error: 'name required' }; 400 { error: 'rotation_interval_days must be >= 1' }; apiErrorResponse-shaped errors otherwise
items.gotchas: This route never accepts a value — setting the actual secret value is a separate call to POST /api/secrets/{id}/value.

items.name: GET /api/secrets/env
items.purpose: Delivers the decrypted env-var bundle for an agent process at startup: every deliverable secret (delivery_enabled + has value), org-wide merged with agent-specific overrides (agent-specific wins by name).
items.auth: x-api-key ONLY — explicitly rejects browser/session principals even if admin; detected by presence of the x-api-key header. Also rejects readonly-role API keys.
items.errors: 503 if ENCRYPTION_KEY missing in production; 403 if not an API-key principal; 403 if role === 'readonly'; 400 { error: 'agent_id required' }; apiErrorResponse-shaped otherwise
items.gotchas: The ONLY endpoint that ever returns plaintext secret values, and only to API-key (non-readonly) principals. Every delivery is audit-logged via logActivity (names + agent_id only, never values). One corrupt row is skipped rather than failing the whole bundle (per repo comment).

items.name: GET /api/secrets/rotation-due
items.purpose: Lists managed secrets whose rotation is due within a given window.
items.auth: x-api-key
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped (SECRETS_DUE)
items.gotchas: No value/plaintext exposure — same metadata-only shape as GET /api/secrets.

items.name: PATCH /api/secrets/{id}
items.purpose: Updates non-value secret metadata: last_rotated_at, rotation_interval_days, notes.
items.auth: x-api-key — deliberately member-reachable (not admin-gated), so the MCP dashclaw_secret_mark_rotated tool can call it
items.errors: 400 { error: '...cannot be changed via PATCH; use POST /api/secrets/{id}/value (admin only)' } if body.value or body.delivery_enabled is present; 404 { error: 'not_found' }; apiErrorResponse-shaped otherwise
items.gotchas: Route explicitly blocks value/delivery_enabled changes here by design — those require the separate admin-only value endpoint. This is the route memory calls out as 'member-reachable on purpose'.

items.name: DELETE /api/secrets/{id}
items.purpose: Deletes a managed secret record.
items.auth: x-api-key + operator/admin (getOrgRole(req) !== 'admin' -> 403)
items.errors: 403 { error: 'Admin access required to delete secrets' }; 404 { error: 'not_found' }; apiErrorResponse-shaped otherwise
items.gotchas: Deletes the row (and its encrypted value, if any) permanently — no soft-delete/undo visible in the route.

items.name: POST /api/secrets/{id}/value
items.purpose: Sets, clears, or configures delivery for a managed secret's plaintext value. This is the ONLY write path for the value; there is no GET on this resource — the value can never be read back, not even by admins (write-only by design).
items.auth: x-api-key + operator/admin (getOrgRole(req) !== 'admin' -> 403)

inputs.body.value: string (1..8192 chars) to set, or null to clear — at least one of value/delivery_enabled required
inputs.body.delivery_enabled: boolean, optional rider — can be set alone or alongside value

items.response: { id, name, has_value, delivery_enabled: 0|1, value_set_at } — NEVER includes the value itself, even in the same-request response confirming it was just set
items.errors: 503 if ENCRYPTION_KEY missing in production; 403 not-admin; 400 if neither value nor delivery_enabled provided; 400 if value fails length/type validation; 400 if delivery_enabled is enabled but the secret name isn't env-var-safe (must match ^[A-Za-z…
items.gotchas: Confirms per project memory: NO GET method exists on this route at all — write-only is enforced structurally (no read handler), not just by convention. Enabling delivery requires the secret name to be a legal env-var identifier since delivered values become process env vars. Every set/clear/delivery-change is audit-logged with name+id only, never the value.

items.name: POST /api/marketing/event
items.purpose: Record anonymous marketing-funnel telemetry events (allowlisted event names) to Redis for the marketing site.
items.auth: public — listed in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES ('/api/marketing'); no API key or session required

inputs.body.event: string, required, must be one of: marketing_hero_cta_clicked, marketing_github_clicked, marketing_demo_evaluated, marketing_self_host_visited, marketing_proof_visited, marketing_vs_section_viewed
inputs.body.properties: flat object, optional, max 8 keys, each string value ≤200 bytes; number/boolean allowed

items.response: 202 { ok: true } — always, regardless of whether Redis actually persisted
items.errors: 400 'invalid_json'; 400 'unknown_event'; 400 with properties validation error string
items.gotchas: No PII/cookies/third-party trackers; response is intentionally uninformative about Redis persistence so clients can't infer server config; rate limit + 2MB body cap still apply via standard middleware path; ip read from x-client-ip header set by middleware, not directly from the request.

items.name: POST /api/mcp
items.purpose: Streamable-HTTP MCP protocol endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0): initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, ping — proxies to DashClawClient/tool+resource handlers.
items.auth: x-api-key (Managed Agents/remote MCP hosts) OR OAuth Bearer token (Claude custom connector, via /api/oauth flow) — both handled by middleware's authenticateProtectedApi/handleBearerAuth; unauthentica…

inputs.body.params: object, method-specific (e.g. { name, arguments } for tools/call; { uri } for resources/read)

items.response: JSON-RPC 2.0 frame: { jsonrpc: '2.0', id, result } (or { error: {code, message} }); notifications/initialized returns 204 No Content per spec
items.errors: -32602 'Unknown tool'/'Unknown resource'; -32601 'Method not found'; -32603 'Internal error' (wrapped as HTTP 500); tool-call errors return isError:true content instead of throwing
items.gotchas: OAuth Bearer callers get a hardcoded agentId 'claude-desktop' identity (not caller-chosen) — a governance primitive, not a bug; instanceOrigin() self-callback resolution deliberately avoids trusting a spoofed Host header (SSRF/credential-exfil defense) — prefers DASHCLAW_URL then VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL then request Host.

items.name: GET /api/model-strategies
items.purpose: List all model strategies (BYOK provider/model routing configs) for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: { strategies: Array<{ strategy_id, org_id, name, description, config, created_by, created_at, updated_at }> }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error on DB failure
items.gotchas: config is JSON-parsed from a config_json column via safeJsonParse (falls back to {} on parse failure).

items.name: POST /api/model-strategies
items.purpose: Create a new model strategy (provider/model chain + task-mode overrides).
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.name: string, required
inputs.body.config: object, required — validated by validateStrategyConfig (provider chain shape)

items.response: 201 { strategy: {strategy_id, org_id, name, description, config, created_by, created_at, updated_at} }
items.errors: 400 'name is required'; 400 'config is required'; 400 with config-prefixed validation message on invalid config shape; apiErrorResponse on other errors
items.gotchas: config validation errors are distinguished from generic errors by checking message.startsWith('config') — a config-validation message that doesn't start with 'config' would incorrectly fall through to 500.

items.name: GET /api/model-strategies/{strategyId}
items.purpose: Fetch a single model strategy by id.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.errors: 404 'Strategy not found'; apiErrorResponse on other errors
items.gotchas: Scoped by org_id — cross-org strategyId returns 404, not another org's data.

items.name: PATCH /api/model-strategies/{strategyId}
items.purpose: Update fields of an existing model strategy.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.errors: 404 'Strategy not found'; 400 with config-prefixed validation message; apiErrorResponse on other errors
items.gotchas: Same config-validation error detection caveat as POST (message.startsWith('config')).

items.name: DELETE /api/model-strategies/{strategyId}
items.purpose: Delete a model strategy.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.errors: 404 'Strategy not found'; apiErrorResponse on other errors
items.gotchas: No confirmation step — irreversible; any active model-strategy-completion callers referencing this id will start 404ing.

items.name: POST /api/model-strategies/{strategyId}/complete
items.purpose: Execute a chat completion using a model strategy's provider chain (BYOK), with budget caps, provider fallback, and cost tracking.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.task_mode: string, optional — overrides primary provider with strategy.config.taskModes[mode]

items.response: { ...completion result fields (from executeCompletion, includes cost tracking), strategy_id, strategy_name }
items.errors: 404 'Strategy not found'; 400 'messages array is required' / 'Each message must have role and content'; 502 with provider_errors array on full provider-chain failure; apiErrorResponse otherwise
items.gotchas: Resolves BYOK provider credentials from org settings server-side; falls back through the strategy's provider chain on failure before surfacing 502.

items.name: GET /api/oauth/authorize
items.purpose: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint: validates PKCE/client/redirect_uri, requires a logged-in browser session, and renders a minimal HTML consent page.
items.auth: NextAuth session cookie (getToken) — NOT x-api-key; unauthenticated requests redirect to /login. Route itself is public per middleware (/api/oauth prefix self-authenticates)

inputs.query.client_id: string, required — must resolve via DCR-registered client
inputs.query.redirect_uri: string, required — must be in the client's registered redirect_uris

items.response: 200 text/html consent page with a POST-back form (CSP: form-action restricted to self + client's callback origin), or 302 redirect to /login if no session
items.errors: 400 unsupported_response_type / invalid_request (missing PKCE/client/redirect) / invalid_client / invalid_redirect_uri (JSON body)
items.gotchas: This is the Claude custom-connector OAuth AS, not a normal API route — human must have an active NextAuth or local-admin session to reach consent.

items.name: POST /api/oauth/authorize
items.purpose: Consent-page submission: issues a short-lived authorization code bound to the session's org/user and the validated PKCE challenge.
items.auth: NextAuth session cookie (getToken) required; same-origin CSRF check (Origin/Referer must match Host)

inputs.query.same params as GET: response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, state, scope

items.errors: 403 'invalid_request'/cross-origin rejected; 401 'login_required'; 400 same validation errors as GET
items.gotchas: Auth code TTL is 5 minutes; agentId hardcoded to 'claude-desktop' on the stored auth_codes row; 303 (not 307) used deliberately so the browser GETs the callback instead of re-POSTing.

items.name: GET /api/oauth/metadata/authorization-server
items.purpose: RFC 8414 OAuth Authorization Server Metadata discovery document.
items.auth: public (no auth) — OAuth discovery must be reachable unauthenticated
items.response: { issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, registration_endpoint, response_types_supported: ['code'], grant_types_supported: ['authorization_code','refresh_token'], code_challenge_methods_supported: ['S256'], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ['none'], scopes_supported: ['governance:read','governance:write'] }
items.errors: none — always 200
items.gotchas: issuerBase() prefers DASHCLAW_URL, then falls back to request Host — self-host operators behind a proxy that forwards an arbitrary Host should set DASHCLAW_URL explicitly; aliased at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server via middleware+next.config rewrite.

items.name: GET /api/oauth/metadata/protected-resource
items.purpose: RFC 9728 OAuth Protected Resource Metadata document, identifying /api/mcp as the protected resource.
items.auth: public (no auth)
items.errors: none — always 200
items.gotchas: Aliased at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource; used by mcpAuthChallenge's WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer.

items.name: POST /api/oauth/register
items.purpose: OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) — open registration, no auth required, for MCP/connector clients.
