items.errors: 400 validation errors (from validateX402Purchase); 404 'Unknown provider_id'/'Unknown endpoint_id' for this org; 400 provider not active / endpoint disabled / endpoint-provider mismatch; 403 guard block (also returned for a post-insert budget-breach…
items.gotchas: Enforced spend = max(declared spend_amount, resolved endpoint default_price) — a purchase can't under-declare against a known-priced endpoint; idempotency short-circuits on (org_id, idempotency_key) before any guard/DB work; if the purchase-detail insert fails after the action record was created, the action is compensating-deleted (Neon HTTP has no multi-statement transactions); AFTER commit, ver…

items.name: GET /api/stream
items.purpose: Server-Sent Events feed of org events (actions, messages, policy updates, decisions, loops, goals, signals, token usage) with replay-from-cursor support.
items.auth: x-api-key (standard middleware auth); demo mode is forwarded through with a synthetic org_demo/admin header pair rather than blocked

inputs.query.lastEventId: optional cursor, also accepted via Last-Event-ID header

items.response: text/event-stream; named SSE events (action_created, message_created, policy_updated, decision_created, guard_decision_created, loop_created/updated, goal_created/updated, signal_detected, token_usage) each with a payload + cursor id; an initial 'connected' event reports replay stats
items.errors: 503 'Realtime backend unavailable' if realtime health check fails; 500 'Internal Server Error' on unexpected throw
items.gotchas: 15s heartbeat comments keep proxies from killing the connection; hard 30-minute max connection duration (auto-closes); dedupes by cursor with a 10k-entry seen-set that clears when full; replay runs after the Response is returned (avoids backpressure deadlock) and live events are buffered until replay completes.

items.name: POST /api/telegram/webhook
items.purpose: Telegram bot webhook handling inline-keyboard approve/deny callback presses on pending-approval action notifications.
items.auth: NOT x-api-key — verifies x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token header (timing-safe compare against TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) plus a sender chat_id allowlist against TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID; public route (lis…

inputs.body: Telegram Update JSON; only callback_query is handled, callback_query.data must match /^(ap|dn):(act_[a-z0-9_-]{1,57})$/

items.response: { ok: true } for all handled/ignored cases (Telegram doesn't need the outcome — feedback goes back via editMessageText on the original message)
items.errors: 401 Unauthorized (bad secret token or sender not the allowlisted admin chat, same status for both to avoid revealing which check failed); 400 Invalid JSON
items.gotchas: TELEGRAM_APPROVER_ORG_ID must be set or it edits the Telegram message with a misconfiguration warning and returns ok; callback is ack'd immediately (answerCallbackQuery) before DB work so Telegram doesn't retry on slow queries; chat_id used for edits is always the trusted admin env var, never the body-provided one; recordApproval returning null (already resolved by another channel) is handled dis…

items.name: GET /api/usage
items.purpose: Return the org's plan, plan limits, current usage counters, and subscription/billing status.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No role gate — any authenticated caller.
items.response: { plan, limits: {...from getPlanLimits}, usage: {...from getUsage}, subscription: { status, current_period_end, trial_ends_at, has_stripe: boolean }, stripe_configured: boolean }
items.errors: 404 if organization not found (unless self-host, see gotchas); 500 on other errors.
items.gotchas: Handles two self-host degradation cases: (1) if the `organizations` table doesn't exist yet (Postgres error code 42P01) and self-host mode is enabled, treats it as zero rows rather than erroring; (2) if the org row itself is missing in self-host mode, returns synthetic free-plan defaults (limits from getPlanLimits('free'), empty usage, active subscription status, has_stripe:false) instead of a 40…

items.name: GET /api/usage/costs
items.purpose: Return a monthly cost breakdown (by action_type), daily cost/action series, and totals for the org's action_records, for a given billing period.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No role gate.

inputs.query.period: string, optional, format YYYY-MM, defaults to getCurrentPeriod(); rejected with 400 if malformed

items.response: { period, total_cost_usd: number (rounded to 3dp), total_actions: number, breakdown: { [action_type]: { count, cost_usd } }, daily: [{ date, actions, cost_usd }] }
items.errors: 400 with code INVALID_PERIOD if period doesn't match /^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/; otherwise apiErrorResponse(error, 'USAGE_COSTS') for uncaught errors.
items.gotchas: Only counts action_records where cost_estimate > 0 in the breakdown query (but totals/daily include all cost_estimate values, zero or not). Period validation exists specifically to avoid an opaque Postgres 500 from a bogus date literal — confirmed by an inline code comment.

items.name: DELETE /api/webhooks
items.purpose: Delete a webhook by id.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role.
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if id missing/malformed; 404 if webhook not found for this org; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: Logs 'webhook.deleted' audit activity. Lookup/delete is scoped to (webhookId, orgId) so cross-tenant deletion isn't possible even with a guessed id.

items.name: GET /api/webhooks
items.purpose: List all webhooks configured for the org, with secrets masked.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No role gate — any org member can list webhooks (secrets are masked for everyone).
items.response: { webhooks: [{...row, secret: '••••••••••••••••••••••••••••XXXX' (partially masked, last 2 chars always hidden) or null}] }
items.errors: 500 on unexpected error.
items.gotchas: Secret masking reveals 4 characters (positions -6 to -2 from the end) while always hiding the final 2 characters, so the full secret is never fully reconstructable from this response even in fragments.

items.name: POST /api/webhooks
items.purpose: Register a new webhook destination for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'.

inputs.body.events: string[], optional, default ['all']; each must be one of the VALID_EVENT_TYPES list (all, autonomy_spike, high_impact_low_oversight, repeated_failures, stale_loop, assumption_drift, stale_assumption,…

items.response: 201 { webhook: { id, url, secret (raw, shown once), events, active: 1, created_at }, storageWarning: string }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if URL invalid (message from isValidWebhookUrl) or events empty/not-an-array/contains an invalid type; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: The signing secret (32 random bytes hex) is returned in full only on this create call — GET /api/webhooks masks it afterward. Logs 'webhook.created' audit activity with url+events.

items.name: GET /api/webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries
items.purpose: List recent delivery attempts (with status/response info) for a specific webhook.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No role gate — any org member can view delivery history.
items.response: { deliveries: [...] } — includes payload and response_body fields, which are redacted at write time (not at read time) per an inline code comment referencing redactForStorage in app/lib/webhooks.ts.
items.errors: 400 if webhookId malformed; 404 if webhook not found for this org; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: payload/response_body are safe to expose here because sensitive data was already redacted when the delivery was logged (logWebhookDelivery), not filtered at read time — so if redaction logic there ever regresses, this endpoint would expose it.

items.name: POST /api/webhooks/{webhookId}/test
items.purpose: Send a synthetic test payload to a webhook's configured URL to verify it's receiving events, using the real HMAC delivery pipeline (deliverWebhook).
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role.
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if webhookId malformed; 404 if webhook not found for this org; 500 on unexpected error.
items.gotchas: The test payload is a fixed synthetic signal ({ event:'test', signals:[{ type:'test', severity:'amber', ... }] }) delivered through the same deliverWebhook() function used for real events (so it exercises the real HMAC signing + delivery-logging path, not a stub). Logs 'webhook.tested' audit activity with success/status.

items.name: POST /api/webhooks/stripe
items.purpose: Stripe billing webhook receiver — syncs org plan/subscription state on checkout completion, subscription updates/cancellation, and failed payments.
items.auth: NOT x-api-key/session — self-authenticates via Stripe-signature verification (stripe.webhooks.constructEvent against the raw request body using STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET). This route is listed in middlew…

inputs.body: raw Stripe event payload (text, not JSON-parsed by the route directly — passed to stripe.webhooks.constructEvent). Relevant event types: checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated, cus…

items.response: { received: true } on success (200). Or 501 { error: 'Stripe not configured' } / 400 { error: 'Invalid signature' } on failure paths.
items.errors: 501 if STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env vars are missing; 400 if signature verification fails; 500 on other processing errors (event handling is wrapped in a top-level try/catch, unhandled event types fall through the switch's default …
items.gotchas: checkout.session.completed requires session.metadata.org_id and .plan to be set (from checkout session creation elsewhere) — silently no-ops (break) if either is missing, no error surfaced. customer.subscription.updated maps Stripe price ID -> plan via PRICE_TO_PLAN, built from STRIPE_PRICE_PRO/STRIPE_PRICE_BUSINESS env vars; if the price isn't mapped, plan is left unchanged but subscription_stat…

items.name: GET /api/widget/summary
items.purpose: Composes one partial-failure-tolerant payload (recent actions, pending approvals, signals, 1-day spend, agents) for the desktop status widget.
items.auth: x-api-key (standard middleware auth); route additionally hard-requires the x-org-id header itself (401 if absent) rather than falling back to org_default like getOrgId does elsewhere
items.response: buildWidgetSummary(...) output plus { degraded: boolean } — degraded is true if any of the 5 underlying sources (recent actions, pending approvals, signals, cost aggregation, agents) failed and fell back to a safe default
items.errors: 401 'Missing organization context' if x-org-id header missing; 500 via apiErrorResponse on total failure
items.gotchas: Each of the 5 data sources is Promise.all'd with its own .catch() — one slow/broken source degrades the widget instead of 500ing the whole response.

items.name: GET /api/workspace/export
items.purpose: Downloads a portable JSON bundle of the org's durable governance record (roadmap v7.2 'workspace carry-out'), for later import into an owned instance.
items.auth: x-api-key (standard middleware auth) PLUS in-route admin gate: requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'
items.response: the workspace bundle object (exported_at + governance data); served with content-disposition attachment filename dashclaw-workspace-{org}-{date}.json
items.errors: 403 'Admin access required'; 500 'Internal server error'
items.gotchas: Never contains credentials/secret values by design; first successful export of a hosted trial org stamps it as 'graduated' (stampTrialExported) — this is a funnel-truth side effect, not just a read.

items.name: POST /api/workspace/import
items.purpose: Ingests a workspace export bundle into the CURRENT org, idempotently (per-table dedupe keys, org-scoped).
items.auth: x-api-key (standard middleware auth) PLUS in-route admin gate: requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'

inputs.body: the JSON bundle produced by GET /api/workspace/export

items.errors: 403 'Admin access required'; 400 'Body must be a workspace bundle (JSON)' (invalid JSON) or a BundleValidationError message
items.gotchas: Re-importing the same bundle is safe — rows already present are skipped, not duplicated or overwritten; API keys/OAuth tokens/secret values are never part of a bundle so they can't be re-imported this way.

package.name: dashclaw
package.description: Minimal governance runtime for AI agents. Intercept, govern, and verify agent actions.
package.moduleSystem: ESM-first (type: module). ESM entry: dashclaw.js; CJS entry: index.cjs (a lazy async bridge that dynamically imports the ESM module; error classes use a Symbol.hasInstance placeholder pattern so instanceof works across the ESM/CJS boundary). Zero runtime dependencies.

..note: Canonical client. Named exports: DashClaw, ApprovalDeniedError, GuardBlockedError, scrubAct.

./legacy.note: DEPRECATED compatibility layer (legacy v1 client). Removed in v5.0.0. Do not target for new work; exists only for older integrations and older method shapes. v1-only methods per README: createWebhook, getActivityLogs, mapCompliance, getProofReport, plus admin identity reads (getPairing, registerIdentity, getIdentities) and flat capability wrappers.

bin.note: npx dashclaw <args> is a pure forwarding shim: spawns npm exec --yes -- @dashclaw/cli <args>. The SDK package owns the bare npm name but the real CLI lives in @dashclaw/cli. Not a programmatic API surface.

constructor.signature: new DashClaw({ baseUrl, apiKey, agentId, agentName?, authToken? })

baseUrl.meaning: DashClaw instance base URL (trailing slash stripped). Constructor throws "baseUrl is required" if missing.

apiKey.meaning: API key sent as x-api-key header on every request. Constructor throws if missing.

agentId.meaning: Unique identifier for this agent; auto-injected into guard/createAction/messages/etc. Constructor throws if missing.

agentName.meaning: Human-readable label stored in the audit trail for attribution.

authToken.meaning: Phase 2 cryptographic attribution: a JWT from your OIDC provider, sent as Authorization: Bearer. Server verifies via JWKS; the JWT sub claim overrides agentId in the audit record when verification succeeds. Guard responses then carry verification_status (verified|unverified|expired|failed|unknown_issuer).

constructor.envConvention: The SDK itself reads NO env vars — you wire them yourself. Conventional names used across README/docs/CLI: DASHCLAW_BASE_URL (or DASHCLAW_URL in MCP contexts), DASHCLAW_API_KEY, optional DASHCLAW_AGENT_ID. The @dashclaw/cli resolves env vars -> ~/.dashclaw/config.json -> interactive prompt.
constructor.namespaces: constructor also builds claw.execution.capabilities.{list,create,get,update,invoke,test,getHealth,listHealth,getHistory} — thin arrows onto the flat listCapabilities/createCapability/... methods. The namespaced paths are the canonical target for new capability work.

errorHandling.model: All HTTP calls go through a single _request helper. Non-OK responses throw. Two custom error classes are exported; everything else surfaces as a plain Error with extra fields.
errorHandling.GuardBlockedError: Thrown by ANY SDK call when the server returns HTTP 403 with { decision: { decision: "block" } } — the request-level policy block. NOTE: a guard() call that returns { decision: "block" } in a 200 body does NOT throw; check decision.decision yourself and throw new GuardBlockedError(decision) to abort. Also thrown by runGoverned()/guardedFetch() when guard returns block. Fields: .name, .message (decision.reason), .decision.
errorHandling.ApprovalDeniedError: Thrown by waitForApproval() (and runGoverned/guardedFetch when they wait) when an operator denies the action (status becomes failed or cancelled) or the approval expires server-side (status expired — check err.status to distinguish). Fields: .name, .message, .decision (the action).
errorHandling.genericErrors: Other non-OK responses throw new Error(data.reason || data.error || "Request failed with status N") with .status (HTTP status), .details, and .decision (full body) attached. Non-JSON error bodies (gateway 502/504/413/429 pages) are parsed defensively to {} so the status-bearing error still throws instead of a SyntaxError.
errorHandling.timeouts: waitForApproval throws a plain Error("Approval timeout after Nms") after options.timeout (default 300000 ms). waitForPairing throws on expiry/timeout.

package.transportNotes: waitForApproval prefers an SSE connection to GET /api/stream (event action.updated scoped to the actionId) and falls back to HTTP polling of GET /api/actions/:id every interval ms (default 5000). Query params with undefined/null values are skipped (never serialized as literal "undefined").

helperExports.scrubAct: Pure function (also applied automatically before any act payload is sent): returns a scrubbed deep copy of an act payload — drops Authorization/Cookie/x-api-key headers and masks common credential token shapes and password=/token=/secret= substrings in command/statement/body_excerpt/content_excerpt. Exported for unit testing; server still re-redacts (defense in depth).

legacySubpath.guidance: Compatibility layer only. Use solely when you need methods not yet promoted to the canonical client. New product work targets the main dashclaw client (and claw.execution.capabilities.* for capability work).

package.relatedPackagesNotInThisInventory: @dashclaw/cli (terminal approvals, doctor, env injection), @dashclaw/mcp-server (33 MCP tools / 6 resources), @dashclaw/openclaw-plugin, @dashclaw/governance skill. Server-side agent-runtime route families (handoffs, operator secrets metadata, skill scan, posture) are deliberately NOT exposed as claw.* methods.

items.name: DashClaw.constructor
items.statusEvidence: authToken is explicitly marked 'Phase 2' in its JSDoc, but the constructor itself carries no phase/deprecation marker — no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.interface: constructor({ baseUrl, apiKey, agentId, agentName, authToken })
items.purpose: Constructs the SDK client. Every other method reads baseUrl/apiKey/agentId off `this`, so this must run first with valid required options.

inputs.baseUrl: string, required — DashClaw base URL; trailing slash stripped
inputs.apiKey: string, required — sent as x-api-key header on every request
inputs.agentId: string, required — this client's agent identity, defaulted into most payloads
inputs.agentName: string, optional — human-readable label stored for audit attribution
inputs.authToken: string, optional — Phase 2 JWT bearer token from an OIDC provider; sent as Authorization: Bearer; server verifies via JWKS and returns verification_status on guard()

items.response: a DashClaw instance with baseUrl/apiKey/agentId/agentName/authToken set and an `execution.capabilities` namespace wired to the capability methods
items.gotchas: Throws synchronously (not a rejected Promise) if baseUrl, apiKey, or agentId is falsy. authToken is a Phase 2 feature — when set, guard() responses carry verification_status (verified/unverified/expired/failed/unknown_issuer); the JWT `sub` claim overrides agentId in the audit record on successful verification.

items.name: client.guard
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.interface: guard(context): Promise<{ decision, reason, signals, verification_status, agent_id, agent_name }>
items.purpose: The core 'Can I do X?' policy check every governed action should call before acting. Also runs non-fabrication verification when content+sourceOfTruth are supplied.

inputs.context: object, required — arbitrary guard context; agent_id/agent_name default from the client if omitted
inputs.context.content: string, optional — outbound content to fabrication-check, pairs with sourceOfTruth
inputs.context.sourceOfTruth: object, optional — { allowedFacts, requiredFacts, forbiddenPatterns?, extract? } the content is allowed to state
inputs.context.act: object, optional — evidence-first act payload ({ kind, command/request/statement/file }) the server evidence-classifies

items.response: { decision: 'allow'|'block'|'require_approval'|'warn', reason, signals: string[], verification_status, agent_id, agent_name }
items.gotchas: Always injects approval_wait_seconds: 300 unless the caller overrides it in context, so a require_approval decision gets a truthful approval_expires_at. verification_status reflects JWT cryptographic verification only if authToken was set on the constructor.

items.name: client.createAction
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: Records 'I am attempting X' in the action ledger. Optionally links to a session via session_id and runs non-fabrication checks like guard().

inputs.action: object, required — action fields (action_type, declared_goal, risk_score, session_id?, content?, sourceOfTruth?, idempotency_key?, ...); agent_id is always overwritten with this.agentId

items.response: { action: Object, action_id: string } — the created action row and its id
items.gotchas: Auto-derives idempotency_key via deriveIdempotencyKey() when the caller doesn't supply one, bucketed by agent_id+action_type+declared_goal+session_id+hour — a blind retry within the same hour returns the original row instead of duplicating. Also defaults approval_wait_seconds: 300 like guard().

items.name: client.runGoverned
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: One-call full governance loop: guard (with act) then createAction, then waitForApproval if pending_approval and wait!==false, then run fn(), then report a one-shot completed/failed outcome. The recommended entry point for governing a single unit of work end-to-end.

inputs.act: object, required — { kind: 'shell'|'http'|'sql'|'file', ... } evidence payload; scrubbed client-side via scrubAct before send
inputs.params: object, optional — context/action fields (action_type, declared_goal, risk_score, ...); `wait` (default true) controls whether to block on pending approval
inputs.fn: function, required — the real work to run once guard/approval clears; its return value is the resolved value

items.endpoint: N/A (local helper, no HTTP call) — internally calls POST /api/guard, POST /api/actions, GET/SSE /api/actions/:id (via waitForApproval), and POST /api/actions/:id/outcome
items.gotchas: Throws GuardBlockedError immediately if guard() returns decision:'block' (createAction is never called in that case). If fn() throws, reportActionOutcome is called with status:'failed' and the error message, then the original error is re-thrown. Passing wait:false skips waitForApproval — caller must poll separately.

items.name: client.guardedFetch
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: runGoverned() wrapped around a real fetch() call — derives an http-kind act (method/url/body_excerpt) automatically so outbound HTTP calls are evidence-classified by the server instead of trusting a self-declared action_type.

inputs.init: object, optional — standard fetch() init (method, headers, body, ...)
inputs.params: object, optional — same shape as runGoverned's params; action_type defaults to 'api', declared_goal defaults to 'HTTP {method} {url}'

items.endpoint: N/A (local helper, no HTTP call itself) — delegates to runGoverned, which hits POST /api/guard, POST /api/actions, POST /api/actions/:id/outcome, and the real fetch(url, init)
items.gotchas: body_excerpt is truncated to 4096 chars and url to 2048 chars before being sent as evidence. Only string bodies are captured as body_excerpt (e.g. a FormData/Blob body yields no excerpt).

items.name: client.updateOutcome
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: PATCH-style '(action) X finished with result Y' update on an existing action row. Older/lower-level sibling of reportActionOutcome.

inputs.outcome: object, required — outcome fields; timestamp_end defaults to now() if omitted

items.gotchas: Distinct from the newer reportActionOutcome family (POST /api/actions/:id/outcome), which enforces terminal-state rules (409 if already terminal) — this PATCH endpoint does not appear to have that guard from the SDK's perspective.

items.name: client.getAction
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: Fetch a single action by id — the same endpoint waitForApproval polls internally.
items.response: the action row plus related collections (server-shape passthrough)

items.name: client.recordAssumption

items.name: client.waitForApproval
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: Block until a human approves/denies a pending_approval action. Tries an SSE stream first for near-instant resolution, falling back to polling if SSE is unavailable or errors non-fatally.

inputs.interval: number ms, optional, default 5000 — only used by the polling fallback

items.response: the confirmed GET /api/actions/:id response ({ action, open_loops, assumptions, message_summary }) once approved
items.endpoint: GET /api/stream (SSE, internal `_connectSSE`) with polling fallback via GET /api/actions/:id (internal `_pollForApproval`)
items.gotchas: Throws ApprovalDeniedError on explicit denial/expiry, GuardBlockedError if the SSE stream itself returns 403, and a plain Error on timeout. SSE errors that aren't denial/block/timeout (isApprovalWaitFatal returns false) are swallowed and polling takes over instead of propagating. The polling fallback prints a one-time console banner (via _printApprovalBanner) with a replay URL. A defensive check …

items.purpose: Convenience one-call path to record a SETTLED x402 payment end-to-end (govern + record + mark succeeded + attach on-chain receipt) for agents that pay outside an OpenClaw governance hook (e.g. a Codex/native-shell agentcash wrapper) and must self-report so spend lands on the Spend → x402 view. The server auto-registers the provider from the name/o…

inputs.transaction_hash: string, optional — on-chain tx hash, attached as receipt evidence

items.endpoint: N/A (local helper, no HTTP call itself) — internally calls POST /api/x402/purchases (via recordPurchase), POST /api/actions/:id/outcome (via reportActionSuccess), and POST /api/artifacts (via recordPurchaseResult, only when transaction_hash or request_id is given)
items.gotchas: Only call this for a SETTLED payment — a free quote or a failed call has nothing to record, per the JSDoc. outcome/artifact steps are skipped entirely if the purchase call doesn't yield an actionId (checks both action.action_id and action.id).

items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface (module comment calls it 'defense in depth, not the only redaction layer' since the server still re-redacts)
items.purpose: Pure client-side redaction helper: returns a scrubbed deep copy of an act payload safe to send as guard()/createAction() evidence, stripping Authorization/Cookie/x-api-key headers and masking common secret patterns (oc_live_*, sk-*, ghp_*, Bearer tokens, password/token/secret=value) in command/statement/body_excerpt/file content_excerpt text. Expo…

inputs.act: object|null — { kind, command?, statement?, request?, file? }; non-object/null values are returned unchanged

items.response: a deep-cloned copy of `act` with secret-bearing headers stripped and token-shaped substrings masked
items.gotchas: Not exhaustive — only matches the specific regexes hardcoded in scrubActText (oc_live_, sk-, ghp_, Bearer, password/token/secret=); other secret shapes (e.g. AWS keys, generic API key formats) pass through unmasked. Used internally by runGoverned/guardedFetch on every act before it's sent, so those callers get this protection automatically; callers who build `act` for guard()/createAction() direc…

items.name: GuardBlockedError
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: Thrown whenever a governance check resolves to decision:'block' — from guard(), createAction() (via a 403 response), runGoverned(), or an SSE stream returning 403. Callers catch this specifically to distinguish a policy block from other errors.

inputs.decision: object, required — the decision object from a blocked guard/action response; message defaults to decision.reason or 'Action blocked by policy'

items.response: an Error instance with `.name === 'GuardBlockedError'` and `.decision` set to the passed decision object
items.gotchas: Thrown both synchronously in some code paths (e.g. runGoverned checking decision.decision === 'block') and via the shared throwRequestError() helper on any 403 response whose body has decision.decision === 'block' — so it can surface from many different method calls, not just guard().

items.name: ApprovalDeniedError
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.interface: class ApprovalDeniedError extends Error { constructor(message, decision) }
items.purpose: Thrown by waitForApproval (and internally by evaluateApprovalState) when a pending_approval action resolves to a denial (status failed/cancelled) or expires before a decision is made, rather than being approved.

inputs.decision: string, required — the terminal status that caused this, e.g. 'failed', 'cancelled', or 'expired'

items.response: an Error instance with `.name === 'ApprovalDeniedError'` and `.decision` set to the status string
items.gotchas: `.decision` here holds a status STRING ('failed'|'cancelled'|'expired'), unlike GuardBlockedError where `.decision` holds a full decision OBJECT — don't assume the same shape across the two error classes.

package.name: dashclaw
package.method_count_evidence: 234 public (non-underscore, non-__init__) methods on DashClaw counted via AST parse of client.py; matches README's stated '234 methods' and 'full platform SDK' parity claim.

constructor.signature: DashClaw(base_url, api_key, agent_id, agent_name=None, auth_token=None, swarm_id=None, guard_mode='off', guard_callback=None, hitl_mode='off', private_key=None, auto_recommend='off', recommendation_confidence_min=70, recommendation_callback=None)

params.base_url: str, required (v2) - DashClaw instance URL. Warns (UserWarning) if not https:// and not localhost/127.0.0.1 - API key would go over plaintext.
params.api_key: str, required (v2) - sent as x-api-key header on every request.
params.agent_id: str, required (v2) - default agent identity attached to actions/messages/etc.
params.agent_name: str, optional (v2) - audit-trail attribution; also auto-filled into guard()/heartbeat() payloads.
params.auth_token: str, optional (v2/Phase 2) - JWT bearer token; server verifies via JWKS and overrides agent_id in the audit record with the JWT sub claim on success.
params.swarm_id: str, optional - stored on the instance; not read anywhere else in client.py that this inventory's grep found beyond assignment (no request payload references it) - likely reserved/forward-compat.
params.guard_mode: 'off'|'warn'|'enforce', default 'off' - constructor raises ValueError if not one of these three. NOT documented in README at all.
params.guard_callback: callable, optional - stored on the instance; not documented in README.
params.hitl_mode: 'off'|'wait', default 'off' (v1 only per README) - when 'wait', create_action()/guard() flows block until human approval or raise ApprovalDeniedError.
params.private_key: cryptography RSAPrivateKey object, optional - enables per-action RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/SHA-256 signing (_sign_payload); silently returns None (no signature, prints a warning) if the cryptography package is missing.
params.auto_recommend: 'off'|'warn'|'enforce', default 'off' - constructor raises ValueError if not one of these three. NOT documented in README's constructor examples.
params.recommendation_confidence_min: float 0-100, default 70 - clamped via max(0,min(x,100)); falls back to 70 on any conversion error. NOT documented in README.
params.recommendation_callback: callable, optional - invoked when auto_recommend applies/overrides a recommendation. NOT documented in README.

constructor.gotchas: guard_mode, guard_callback, swarm_id, auto_recommend, recommendation_confidence_min, and recommendation_callback are all real constructor parameters in client.py (lines 100-148) but NONE of them appear in either the 'v2-compatible' or 'Full constructor (v1 extended)' README examples - the README undersells the constructor surface. auto_recommend does appear later in the README's Adaptive Recommendations code sample without ever being introduced as a constructor kwarg.

package.environment_config: No environment-variable auto-loading in client.py itself (unlike the CLI/MCP server) - base_url/api_key/agent_id must be passed explicitly by the calling application, typically read from os.environ by the CALLER (see README examples using os.environ['DASHCLAW_URL'] etc. inside application code, not inside the SDK).

DashClawError.purpose: Base error for all SDK-raised exceptions; carries .status (HTTP status int or None) and .details (parsed error body or None).
DashClawError.raised_by: _raise_normalized_http_error - translates any non-Guard/Approval HTTPError into this, attaching status + parsed JSON body as details.

GuardBlockedError.purpose: Raised when a guard decision is 'block' (run_governed) or when the server's HTTP error body indicates a guard block. Exposes .decision, .reasons, .warnings, .matched_policies, .risk_score pulled from the decision dict. status is hardcoded 403.
GuardBlockedError.raised_by: run_governed() directly on decision['decision']=='block'; also via _raise_normalized_http_error for 403 responses whose body looks like a guard decision.

ApprovalDeniedError.purpose: Raised when a human operator denies a pending action, or when a pending approval expires (decision='expired'). status hardcoded 403.
ApprovalDeniedError.raised_by: wait_for_approval() / run_governed() when the approval resolves to deny or expires.

error_model.notes: No dedicated timeout/network-error class - urllib.error.URLError / socket timeouts propagate as raw Python exceptions (not wrapped in DashClawError). Only HTTPError responses go through _raise_normalized_http_error.

OpenClawAgent (module-level alias `OpenClawAgent = DashClaw` at client.py:2495 - identical class, kept for backward-compat naming from the project's earlier OpenClaw branding)

helpers.name: scrub_act
helpers.purpose: Pure module-level helper: returns a scrubbed deep copy of an `act` payload ({kind, command, request, statement, file}) before it is sent as guard()/create_action() evidence - strips Authorization/Cookie/x-api-key headers and masks oc_live_/sk-/ghp_/Bearer tokens and password=/token=/secret= substrings in text excerpts. Used internally by run_governed(); exported for standalone testing.
helpers.gotchas: Client-side scrub only - defense in depth, not the only redaction layer; the server re-redacts independently per its own docstring note.

integrations.purpose: LangChain callback handler: auto-creates a DashClaw action on on_llm_start/on_tool_start and closes it via update_outcome on _end/_error, plus calls report_token_usage when token_usage is present in llm_output.
integrations.gotchas: Falls back to dummy no-op BaseCallbackHandler/LLMResult classes if langchain-core isn't installed (import wrapped in try/except) - importing this module never hard-fails, but the handler becomes inert. Requires the optional 'langchain' extra (pip install dashclaw[langchain]) for real functionality.

integrations.purpose: CrewAI integration: task_callback logs a completed Task as an action; instrument_agent(agent) monkeypatches agent.execute_task to log start/success/failure with duration.
integrations.statusEvidence: instrument_agent's own docstring says 'Experimental: Patch a CrewAI agent to log step-by-step progress.'
integrations.gotchas: No optional-dependency declared in pyproject.toml for crewai (unlike langchain) - import crewai wrapped in try/except with dummy Agent/Task classes, so importing without crewai installed is safe but non-functional.

integrations.purpose: AutoGen integration: instrument_agent(agent) registers a process_last_received_message hook that logs each received message as a 'message' action.
integrations.gotchas: No optional dependency for autogen in pyproject.toml either. Comment in source notes tool-call hooking isn't implemented ('We could also hook into tool calls if AutoGen exposes them clearly via hooks') - only message reception is instrumented, not tool use.

parity_gaps_vs_node_sdk: Per README: Node v2 SDK is a curated 149-method subset; Python is the 'full platform SDK' at 234 methods (parity with the DEPRECATED, removed-in-v5.0.0 Node v1 legacy SDK).
Node v2 has getLessons (consolidated lesson readback) with NO Python equivalent.

Node v2 has recordPurchaseResult (x402 result snapshot) with NO Python wrapper - Python callers must POST directly to /api/artifacts with artifact_type='x402_purchase_result' (client.py's own record_x402_purchase does this internally via a private _attach_x402_receipt helper, but there is no public standalone method).

Python-only (v1-extended, no Node v2 equivalent per README): createWebhook/getActivityLogs/mapCompliance/getProofReport-style methods, plus the entire Prompt Management, Evaluations/Scorers, Compliance Export/Schedule, Scoring Profiles, Risk Templates, and Auto-Calibration surfaces documented below as undocumented-in-README.
Authoritative matrix lives in docs/sdk-parity.md (not fully cross-checked in this pass; README states it is canonical).
package.undocumented_but_present_note: 94 of 234 public methods have no dedicated README description (no method-table row, no prose walkthrough) - see methods with status='experimental' below. Most fall into five whole subsystems: Prompt Management (12 methods), Evaluations/Scorers (10), Compliance Export/Schedule extras (6), Scoring Profiles + Risk Templates + Auto-Calibrate (17, matching the README parity table's own '(17 scoring/risk methods)' placeholder row that lists no actual names), and Learning Analytics compute-variants (4). These are real, callable, non-private methods in client.py - just missing end-user docs.

package.name: @dashclaw/cli
package.install: npm install -g @dashclaw/cli   (or run ad hoc via `npx dashclaw <command>` / `npx dashclaw up` without a global install)
configResolutionOrder: 2. Saved config at ~/.dashclaw/config.json (mode 600, written by first interactive run or `dashclaw install claude`)
3. Interactive prompt on first run (only when stdin is a TTY); offers to save to ~/.dashclaw/config.json

Env vars always override the saved file. `install`, `codex notify`, and `cost` resolve config non-interactively/optionally (COMMANDS_OPTIONAL_CONFIG) so provisioning doesn't require pre-existing keys.
package.runInstructions: Global: `npm install -g @dashclaw/cli` then `dashclaw <command>`. Zero-install bootstrap of a whole local instance: `npx dashclaw up`. Source: cli/bin/dashclaw.js is the single entrypoint; all commands route through COMMAND_HANDLERS in that file.

items.name: dashclaw up
items.statusEvidence: Core onboarding path documented in README.md and referenced throughout MEMORY.md (v4.63.x 'first-run reliability' ships); has a full checkpoint/resume state machine (lib/up/instance.js STEPS) and dedicated test suite (test/up/*.test.js).
items.purpose: One-command, resumable installer/launcher: fetches the platform release, installs deps, provisions a database (Docker/embedded/URL), runs migrations + creates the first admin, builds, starts the Next.js server, offers to connect Claude Code, and opens /setup in a browser.

inputs.--update: Re-fetch + rebuild from the latest published/GitHub-release version (resets the resumable instance.json checkpoint)
inputs.--yes: Non-interactive: auto-picks DB mode (docker if available else embedded) and auto-connects Claude Code without prompting
inputs.--db docker|embedded|url: Force a database mode; 'url' prompts for a postgresql:// connection string
inputs.--port <n>: Server port, integer 1-65535 (default: 3000, or the previously saved port on resume)
inputs.--no-browser: Do not open the browser to /setup when the server is ready
inputs.--source-dir <path>: Use a local repo checkout instead of downloading the published tarball (skips version resolution)

items.gotchas: Resolves the platform version from GitHub Releases first (api.github.com/repos/ucsandman/DashClaw/releases/latest, verified via a HEAD check on the tag's tarball), falling back to npm's `dashclaw` package version only on GitHub API failure — npm lags on platform-only releases because SDKs republish only when SDK source changes (see cli/lib/up/fetch-app.js comment, and MEMORY.md 'DASHCLAW_URL brea…

items.name: dashclaw down
items.statusEvidence: Paired with `up` in bin/dashclaw.js COMMAND_HANDLERS and covered by test/up/orchestrator.test.js.
items.purpose: Stops the locally started server (kill by recorded pid) and stops the Docker Postgres container if `up` started one in docker mode. Embedded Postgres dies with the `up` process, so there is nothing to stop for that mode.

inputs.--dir <path>: Target the state directory used by a non-default `up --dir` install (default: ~/.dashclaw)

items.gotchas: Only stops what instance.json recorded; if the server was started outside `dashclaw up` (or the pid file is stale), it has nothing to kill.

items.name: dashclaw import <bundle.json>
items.statusEvidence: Comment in bin/dashclaw.js labels it 'v7.2 graduation path'; MEMORY.md confirms 'v7.2 graduation path SHIPPED v4.65.0'.
items.purpose: Imports policies, guard decisions, action records, open loops, assumptions, and agent identities from an exported bundle into the configured instance via POST /api/workspace/import.
items.gotchas: Idempotent — re-running skips rows that already exist (reports imported/skipped counts per table). API keys, OAuth tokens, and secret values never ride a bundle by design.

items.name: dashclaw approvals
items.statusEvidence: In COMMANDS_NEEDING_CONFIG; full render/key-handling implementation in bin/dashclaw.js (cmdApprovals and its helpers).
items.purpose: Interactive full-screen TUI inbox of pending approval requests with live SSE push updates; arrow keys navigate, A approves, D denies, O opens the replay URL in a browser, Q quits, R refreshes.
items.gotchas: Requires a real TTY (ensureApprovalTty exits with an error otherwise) — use `dashclaw approve`/`dashclaw deny` for scripts/CI. SSE stream failures fail soft to manual refresh via R.

items.name: dashclaw halt on|off|status
items.statusEvidence: README documents propagation time (~3s across instances) and links docs/architecture/enforcement-boundary.md; requires admin API key (401/403 handled explicitly).
items.purpose: Org-wide kill switch via GET/POST /api/halt: `on` makes every governed action for the org resolve to block immediately, `off` resumes normal guard evaluation, `status` reports who halted, why, and since when.

inputs.--reason <text>: Reason recorded with `halt on` (ignored for off/status)

items.gotchas: Halt is a decision-layer switch — whether a blocked action is mechanically stopped depends on the surface, not guaranteed by the halt itself (see enforcement-boundary.md). Needs an admin-scoped API key; a non-admin key gets 'Rejected (admin access required)'.

items.name: dashclaw doctor
items.statusEvidence: README explicitly documents a behavior change ('Changed in 0.4.0: no longer applies remote auto-fixes by default'), indicating an established, versioned feature.
items.purpose: Diagnoses both the remote DashClaw instance (GET /api/doctor: database, config, auth, deployment, SDK reachability, governance, data hygiene) and this local machine (stale compiled mcp-server/lib, .gitattributes drift, local DB schema behind code, disabled OpenClaw plugin, stale CLI shim, broken Claude hook installs, leaked machine-scope DASHCLAW_…

inputs.--fix: Apply safe auto-fixes (local + remote via POST /api/doctor/fix), then re-check and print what changed
inputs.--json: JSON output (includes local checks) for CI/scripts
inputs.--no-fix: Accepted no-op alias — report-only is already the default; wins over --fix if both are passed
inputs.--category <list>: Comma-separated filter for remote checks (e.g. database,config)
inputs.--repo <path>: Treat <path> as the DashClaw checkout for local repo-shape checks instead of auto-detecting

items.gotchas: Report-only by default since v0.4.0 — --fix is required to apply anything. Detect-only classes (leaked env vars, OpenClaw configs) are never auto-fixed even with --fix, only reported with remediation text. Exit code 1 on any warn/fail, 0 only when fully healthy.

items.name: dashclaw code ingest
items.statusEvidence: Documented in README with size limits, retry/backoff, and compression behavior; has dedicated test/code/ingest.test.js.
items.purpose: Backfills Claude Code session transcripts: walks ~/.claude/projects (or override), stream-reads each .jsonl, and POSTs it to /api/code-sessions/ingest-jsonl for the server's canonical parser to process.

inputs.--dry-run: Preview the file list and payload shape without POSTing

config.note: org_id is NOT required for MCP. Governance tools (33) + the 3 DASHCLAW_GATED_TOOLS (dashclaw_status, dashclaw_recent_decisions, export_dashclaw_evidence) register only when both DASHCLAW_URL and DASHCLAW_API_KEY are set (registration.ts governanceEnabled()). Each provider's ~82 tools register only when that provider's credential env var(s) are present, OR a stored connection's custom envVar is present (registration.ts providerEnabled()/credentialEnvCandidates() — Stripe uniquely accepts either STRIPE_TEST_SECRET_KEY or STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET_KEY). All other local-context/policy/audit/launch-plan tools (~33) always register.

registration.claude_code_stdio: npx -y @dashclaw/mcp-server --url https://your-dashclaw.vercel.app --key oc_live_xxx --agent-id claude-code   — or in .mcp.json: { "mcpServers": { "dashclaw": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@dashclaw/mcp-server"], "env": { "DASHCLAW_URL": "https://your-dashclaw.vercel.app", "DASHCLAW_API_KEY": "oc_live_xxx", "DASHCLAW_AGENT_ID": "claude-code" } } } }
registration.claude_desktop: stdio is NOT supported for Desktop main chat (crashes on Desktop's bundled Node; the old one-click .mcpb bundle is retired). Use the OAuth custom connector instead: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste https://<instance>/api/mcp; Claude discovers /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, registers via DCR, and opens the DashClaw login + consent screen. No API key entered in the UI. Works on Free (capped at 1 custom connector)/Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise.
registration.claude_managed_agents: Streamable HTTP at POST https://<instance>/api/mcp with header x-api-key: oc_live_xxx, passed via mcp_servers:[{type:'url', url, headers, name:'dashclaw'}] on client.beta.agents.create(...). Each HTTP request is stateless (no ambient session id auto-stamping across calls, unlike stdio).
registration.plugin_marketplace: Claude app → Customize → Plugins → "+" → Add marketplace → github: ucsandman/DashClaw, then install the `dashclaw` plugin to load the governance-protocol + platform-intelligence skills alongside the MCP tools.

items.name: dashclaw_pretool.py
items.statusEvidence: Docstring labeled 'PreToolUse Hook v2 for Claude Code'; evaluates 40+ tool calls via the dashclaw_agent_intel classifier; wired in hooks.json with a 3660s timeout (the field is seconds; a ms-scale value overflows the harness timer and cancels the hook, failing open - fixed v4.72.1) so the hook's own 3600s approval wait always resolves first.
items.interface: hooks.json PreToolUse, matcher `Agent|Task|Bash|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Skill|mcp__.*`, invoked via `node run_hook.cjs dashclaw_pretool.py`
items.purpose: Guards every governed tool call against DashClaw policy: calls guard(), blocks (exit 2) on `block`, waits on `require_approval`, and records the opened action_id for the Stop hook to close out.
items.gotchas: Exit code 2 blocks the tool call and Claude Code shows stderr to the user; any other non-zero exit is NOT a safe block signal (see run_hook.cjs's comment about why a naive `python3 X || python X` fallback double-fires the hook). Loads .env / .env.local by walking up from the hook file's directory — DASHCLAW_DISABLE_DOTENV is a test-only escape hatch, never set in production.

items.name: dashclaw_posttool.py
items.statusEvidence: Docstring labeled 'PostToolUse Hook v2 for Claude Code'; v2 explicitly adds richer outcome reporting (500-char summaries, structured outcome_metadata, error classification) over a documented v1.
items.interface: hooks.json PostToolUse, matcher `Agent|Task|Bash|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|mcp__.*`, invoked via `node run_hook.cjs dashclaw_posttool.py`
items.purpose: Records the outcome of the action opened by dashclaw_pretool.py — exit_code, error_type classification (timeout/permission/not_found/runtime), and output summary.
items.gotchas: Never blocks — always exits 0, even on internal failure, so it can't be used to enforce policy after the fact. Imports dashclaw_agent_intel.http_client and .behavior_recorder from the sibling module.

items.name: dashclaw_stop.py
items.statusEvidence: Decomposed in the v4.71.0 health pass into dashclaw_agent_intel.stop_transcript / stop_state / stop_uploads with 67 dedicated unit tests plus the existing subprocess suites (never-block, fail-silent, coverage, assumptions).
items.interface: hooks.json Stop (no matcher — fires on every turn end), invoked via `node run_hook.cjs dashclaw_stop.py`
items.purpose: Sums assistant-turn LLM token usage from the session transcript and PATCHes tokens_in/tokens_out/model onto every action_id opened during the turn (evenly distributed); optionally triggers Code Sessions ingest and behavior-insight recording.
items.gotchas: Never blocks (always exits 0). Requires .env/.env.local loading identical to pretool/posttool — the code comment explicitly warns that without it 'the Stop hook silently fails for every session that doesn't inherit vars from the shell — which is most real Claude Code sessions.' Only imports dashclaw_code_session_reporter when DASHCLAW_CODE_SESSIONS_ENABLED is truthy (opt-in, fail-silent import).

items.name: dashclaw_session_digest.py
items.statusEvidence: Docstring states an explicit latency budget (~4.2s across 3 requests) and a documented fail-silent contract; wired in both hooks.json (SessionStart) and cli/lib/codex/install.js's TOML block, confirming cross-runtime parity.
items.interface: hooks.json SessionStart (10s timeout), invoked via `node run_hook.cjs dashclaw_session_digest.py`; also wired by `dashclaw install codex` into ~/.codex/config.toml [[hooks.SessionStart]]
items.purpose: Prints a compact digest (recent decisions, distilled lessons, unconsumed handoff) to stdout at session start; Claude Code/Codex add SessionStart stdout to session context so the agent starts already informed.
items.gotchas: Read-only, fail-silent by design: any missing config, network error, or slow API produces NO output and exit 0 rather than an error. PLUGIN_PARITY.md notes this hook was only wired for Codex in v3.7 item 6 once codex-cli 0.139.0's SessionStart hook event was confirmed to actually fire (PascalCase in config.toml, same convention as the other three events).

items.name: dashclaw_code_session_reporter.py
items.statusEvidence: Docstring: 'Stop-hook helper' — every exit path wrapped in try/except so it never breaks the Stop hook contract; explicitly opt-in gated.
items.interface: Not directly wired in hooks.json — imported by dashclaw_stop.py only when DASHCLAW_CODE_SESSIONS_ENABLED is set
items.purpose: Ships the turn's JSONL transcript slice plus the tool_use→action_id map to POST /api/code-sessions/ingest-jsonl for the Code Sessions feature.

items.name: run_hook.cjs
items.statusEvidence: Extensive inline comment documents the exact failure mode it was built to avoid (a `python3 X || python X` fallback double-firing hooks on an intentional exit-2 block).
items.interface: Node launcher invoked by every hooks.json entry as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run_hook.cjs" <script>.py [args]`
items.purpose: Resolves python3 vs python (probed via `--version`, not just spawnability, to dodge the Windows Store python3 alias stub) exactly once per invocation, then execs the named hook script with stdio passed through and the exit code mirrored.
items.gotchas: If no working Python is found, it exits 0 (proceed-with-notice) rather than blocking the user's tool call — governance is silently skipped for that call, only a stderr notice is printed. Only accepts a bare filename argument (rejects path separators or `..`) as a defense against launcher misuse.
